title.zh: 卷七十七 列傳第六十七 恩倖
title.raw: 卷七十七 列傳第六十七 恩倖 Volume 77 Biographies 67: Noble Favorites

sentences.zh: 戴法興 徐爰 阮佃夫 紀僧真 劉系宗 茹法亮 呂文顯 茹法珍 周石珍 陸驗 司馬申 施文慶 沈客卿 孔範

translations.literal: Dai Faxing, Xu Ai, Ruan Dianfu, Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, Ru Fazhen, Zhou Shizhen, Lu Yan, Sima Shen, Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and Kong Fan
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing, Xu Ai, Ruan Dianfu, Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, Ru Fazhen, Zhou Shizhen, Lu Yan, Sima Shen, Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and Kong Fan

sentences.zh: 夫鮑魚芳蘭，在於所習，中人之性，可以上下。

translations.literal: Now salted fish and fragrant orchids alike depend on what one is accustomed to; the nature of an average person may be raised or lowered.
translations.idiomatic: Just as salted fish and orchids take their character from their surroundings, so too can an ordinary person's nature be elevated or debased by habit.

sentences.zh: 然則謀于管仲，齊桓有邵陵之師，邇于易牙，小白掩陽門之扇。

translations.literal: Thus when he took counsel with Guan Zhong, Duke Huan of Qi had armies at Shaoling; when he drew close to Yi Ya, Duke Huan was shut behind the Yang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Huan of Qi listened to Guan Zhong, he led armies as far as Shaoling; when he grew intimate with Yi Ya, he ended shut in behind the Yang Gate.

sentences.zh: 夫以霸者一身，且有洿隆之別，況下于此，胡可勝言者乎。

translations.literal: If even a hegemon in his own person could sink so low or rise so high, how much more those below him—what need is there to say more?
translations.idiomatic: If a single hegemon's fortunes could sink or soar so sharply, how much more those who stood beneath him—there is scarcely any end to what might be said.

sentences.zh: 故古之哲王，莫不斯慎。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage kings of antiquity were all careful in this regard.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sage kings of old were invariably cautious about such matters.

sentences.zh: 自漢氏以來，年且千祀，而近慣用事，無乏于時，莫不官由近親，情因狎重。

translations.literal: From the Han dynasty onward, nearly a thousand years have passed, yet favorites who held power at court have never been lacking; their offices always came through close association, their influence through intimacy and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han, nearly a thousand years have passed, yet court favorites have never been absent from power—always advanced through proximity, always trusted through long intimacy.

sentences.zh: 至如中書所司，掌在機務。

translations.literal: As for the Secretariat, what it administered was the handling of crucial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat, for its part, held charge of the most sensitive state business.

sentences.zh: 漢元以令、僕用事，魏明以監、令專權，在晉中朝，常為重寄，故公曾之歎，恨於失職。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yuan of Han the director and vice-director held power; under Emperor Ming of Wei the supervisor and director monopolized authority; in the Jin central court the post was often a weighty trust—hence Gong Zeng's lament at losing his office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Han relied on his Secretariat director and vice-director; Emperor Ming of Wei gave sole power to supervisor and director; in the Jin central court the post was repeatedly entrusted with grave responsibility—hence Gong Zeng's bitter regret when he was stripped of it.

sentences.zh: 于時舍人之任，位居九品，江左置通事郎，管司詔誥，其後郎還為侍郎，而舍人亦稱通事。

translations.literal: At that time the duty of palace secretary ranked in the ninth grade; south of the Yangtze they established the post of communications officer to manage imperial edicts, and later when the officer returned to the rank of vice-director, the secretary was also called communications officer.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the palace secretary held ninth-rank status; in the Eastern Jin they created the communications officer to handle edicts, and later, when that officer reverted to vice-director, the secretary title was likewise called communications officer.

sentences.zh: 元帝用琅邪劉超，以謹慎居職。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan employed Liu Chao of Langye, who held the post through his careful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan appointed Liu Chao of Langye, who kept the post through scrupulous diligence.

sentences.zh: 宋文世，秋當、周赳並出寒門。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Wen of Song, Qiu Dang and Zhou Jiu both came from humble families.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Song, Qiu Dang and Zhou Jiu both rose from humble backgrounds.

sentences.zh: 孝武以來，士庶雜選，如東海鮑照以才學知名，又用魯郡巢尚之，江夏王義恭以為非選。

translations.literal: From Emperor Xiaowu onward, gentlemen and commoners were mixed in selection; for example Bao Zhao of Donghai was famed for talent and learning, and Chao Shangzhi of Lu commandery was also employed, though Prince Jiangxia Yigong considered this improper selection.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Xiaowu on, men of gentry and common birth were chosen alike—Bao Zhao of Donghai, renowned for learning, and Chao Shangzhi of Lu, whom Prince Jiangxia Yigong judged an unworthy appointment.

sentences.zh: 帝遣尚之送尚書四十餘牒，宣敕論辯，義恭乃歎曰：「人主誠知人。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent Shangzhi to deliver more than forty memorials from the Secretariat, to proclaim edicts and debate issues; Yigong then sighed and said, "The sovereign truly knows men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Shangzhi deliver over forty Secretariat documents, proclaim edicts, and argue points at court; Yigong sighed and said, "The throne truly knows how to judge men.

sentences.zh: 及明帝世，胡母顥、阮佃夫之徒，專為佞幸矣。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Ming, Hu Muhao, Ruan Dianfu, and their like became devoted sycophants and favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming, Hu Muhao, Ruan Dianfu, and men of their kind were nothing but fawning court favorites.

sentences.zh: 齊初亦用久勞及以親信，關讞表啟，發署詔敕，頗涉辭翰者，亦為詔文，侍郎之局復見侵矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi they also employed men of long service and personal trust; they handled legal memorials and reports, issued and signed edicts, and those with some literary skill also drafted imperial documents—the domain of the vice-director was again encroached upon.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qi as well, long-serving confidants handled legal papers and memorials, issued edicts, and those with literary skill drafted proclamations—once again usurping the vice-directors' proper sphere.

sentences.zh: 建武世，詔命始不關中書，專出舍人。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era, edicts and orders no longer passed through the Secretariat but issued solely from the palace secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwu reign, edicts ceased to involve the Secretariat and came exclusively from the palace secretaries.

sentences.zh: 省內舍人四人，所直四省，其下有主書令史，舊用武官，宋改文吏，人數無員，莫非左右要密。

translations.literal: Within the palace there were four secretaries, each responsible for one of the four bureaus; beneath them were chief clerks and recorders—formerly military officers, changed to civil clerks under Song—with no fixed quota, all of them intimate confidants at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Four palace secretaries within the inner palace each oversaw one bureau; below them were chief clerks—once military men, made civil under Song—with no fixed head count, every one a trusted intimate at the ruler's elbow.

sentences.zh: 天下文簿板籍，入副其省，萬機嚴秘，有如尚書外司。

translations.literal: The documents and registers of the realm were filed in duplicate in their bureau; state affairs were kept in strict secrecy, like an outer branch of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Copies of the realm's records were held in their bureau; the most sensitive business was guarded as closely as a secretariat outside the Secretariat itself.

sentences.zh: 領武官有制局監、外監，領器仗兵役，亦用寒人。

translations.literal: Military officers in charge included the director of the arsenal bureau and the outer director, who commanded weapons, equipment, and military labor—commoners were employed in these posts as well.
translations.idiomatic: Arsenal directors and outer directors commanded weapons, gear, and corvée troops—and humble-born men filled these posts too.

sentences.zh: 爰及梁、陳，斯風未改。

translations.literal: Down through Liang and Chen, this practice did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Through Liang and Chen, the custom endured unchanged.

sentences.zh: 其四代之被恩幸者，今立以為篇，以繼前史之作云爾。

translations.literal: Those favored with imperial grace in these four dynasties are now set forth in this chapter, to continue the work of the previous histories.
translations.idiomatic: The men who won imperial favor in these four dynasties are gathered here in one chapter, carrying on what earlier histories began.

sentences.zh: 戴法興

translations.literal: Dai Faxing
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing

sentences.zh: 戴法興，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Dai Faxing was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing came from Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 家貧，父碩子以販紵為業。

translations.literal: His family was poor; his father Shuozi made a living selling ramie cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor; his father Shuozi earned a living trading ramie cloth.

sentences.zh: 法興二兄延壽、延興並修立，延壽善書，法興好學。

translations.literal: Faxing's two elder brothers Yanshou and Yanxing were both upright in conduct; Yanshou excelled at calligraphy, and Faxing loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing's elder brothers Yanshou and Yanxing were both men of integrity; Yanshou was a fine calligrapher, and Faxing devoted himself to study.

sentences.zh: 山陰有陳戴者，家富有錢三千萬，鄉人或云：「戴碩子三兒敵陳戴三千萬錢。」

translations.literal: In Shanyin there was a Chen Dai whose family possessed wealth of thirty million cash; people in the district would say, "Shuozi's three sons are a match for Chen Dai's thirty million."
translations.idiomatic: A man named Chen Dai in Shanyin was worth thirty million cash, and locals used to say, "Shuozi's three sons are worth as much as Chen Dai's thirty million."

sentences.zh: 孝武親覽朝政，不任大臣，而腹心耳目不得無所委寄。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu personally reviewed court affairs and did not rely on great ministers, yet his closest confidants and eyes and ears could not be left without someone to entrust.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu personally oversaw government and would not lean on great ministers, yet he still had to place his trust in intimate confidants who served as his eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 法興頗知古今，素見親待，雖出侍東宮，而意任隆密。

translations.literal: Faxing was fairly learned in past and present affairs and had long been treated with personal favor; though he went out to attend the Eastern Palace, the emperor's trust in him remained weighty and close.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing knew history and current affairs well and had long enjoyed the emperor's favor; though he served at the Eastern Palace, the throne's confidence in him remained deep and confidential.

sentences.zh: 魯郡巢尚之，人士之末，元嘉中，侍始興王浚讀書，亦涉獵文史，為上所知。

translations.literal: Chao Shangzhi of Lu commandery stood at the bottom of the gentry; in the Yuanjia era he attended Prince Shixing Jun in his studies, also dipped into literature and history, and came to the emperor's notice.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Shangzhi of Lu was a man of low standing; during Yuanjia he tutored Prince Shixing Jun, read widely in letters and history, and won the emperor's attention.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，補東海國侍郎，仍兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian he was appointed attendant of Donghai kingdom and concurrently palace secretary for communications at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaojian era he became attendant of Donghai and concurrently a Secretariat communications secretary.

sentences.zh: 凡選授遷轉誅賞大處分，上皆與法興、尚之參懷。

translations.literal: For all major decisions on appointments, transfers, promotions, punishments, rewards, and executions, the emperor consulted with Faxing and Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Every major appointment, transfer, reward, punishment, or execution was weighed with Faxing and Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 內外諸雜事多委明寶。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous affairs inside and outside the palace were largely entrusted to Mingbao.
translations.idiomatic: Most routine business, within the palace and beyond, was left to Mingbao.

sentences.zh: 上性嚴暴，睚眥之間，動至罪戮。

translations.literal: The emperor's nature was harsh and violent; over the smallest grudge he would often impose punishment and execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was harsh and violent; the slightest offense could bring punishment or death.

sentences.zh: 尚之每臨事解釋，多得全免，殿省甚賴之。

translations.literal: Whenever matters arose Shangzhi would explain and intercede, and many were fully spared; the palace offices relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi would plead and explain on each occasion, and many were spared entirely—the inner court depended on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 而法興、明寶大通人事，多納貨賄，凡所薦達，言無不行，天下輻湊，門外成市，家產並累千金。

translations.literal: Faxing and Mingbao, however, were thoroughly versed in human affairs and accepted many bribes; whatever they recommended was invariably carried out; the realm converged on them until their gates became a marketplace, and their household wealth amounted to thousands in gold.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing and Mingbao, by contrast, knew every lever of power and took bribes freely; nothing they recommended failed to pass; petitioners thronged their gates like a market, and each household amassed thousands in gold.

sentences.zh: 明寶驕縱尤甚，長子敬為揚州從事，與上爭買禦物。

translations.literal: Mingbao was especially arrogant and unrestrained; his eldest son Jing served as staff officer of Yang province and vied with the emperor in buying imperial goods.
translations.idiomatic: Mingbao was the more arrogant of the two; his eldest son Jing, a Yangzhou staff officer, even competed with the emperor to buy court goods.

sentences.zh: 六宮嘗出，敬盛服騎馬，于車左右馳驟去來。

translations.literal: When the six palaces went out on an excursion, Jing dressed splendidly and rode a horse, galloping back and forth to the left and right of the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial household went abroad, Jing appeared in splendid dress on horseback, dashing to and fro beside the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，賜敬死，系明寶尚方。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious, ordered Jing to die, and imprisoned Mingbao in the imperial workshops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, had Jing put to death, and sent Mingbao to the imperial workshops as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 尋被原釋，委任如初。

translations.literal: Before long he was pardoned and released, and his appointment was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was pardoned and restored to his former trust.

sentences.zh: 孝武崩，前廢帝即位，法興遷越騎校尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died and the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, Faxing was promoted to colonel of the Yue cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu's death, when the Former Deposed Emperor acceded, Faxing was made colonel of the Yue cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時太宰江夏王義恭錄尚書事，任同總己，而法興、尚之執權日久，威行內外，義恭積相畏服，至是懾憚尤甚。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia Yigong recorded Secretariat affairs with authority equal to holding all power himself, yet Faxing and Shangzhi had held power for so long that their prestige ruled inside and outside the court; Yigong had long feared and submitted to them, and now he was especially awed and intimidated.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince Jiangxia Yigong then oversaw the Secretariat with powers nearly equal to the throne itself, but Faxing and Shangzhi had ruled so long that their authority reached everywhere; Yigong had feared them for years and now stood in still greater awe.

sentences.zh: 廢帝未親萬機，凡詔敕施為，悉決法興之手，尚書中事無大小專斷之，顏師伯、義恭守空名而已。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor did not personally handle state affairs; all edicts and measures were decided in Faxing's hands, and nothing great or small in the Secretariat escaped his sole judgment—Yan Shibo and Yigong kept empty titles only.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor did not yet govern in person; every edict and act of state passed through Faxing, who decided all Secretariat business large and small—Yan Shibo and Yigong held nothing but hollow titles.

sentences.zh: 尚之甚聰敏，時百姓欲為孝武立寺，疑其名。

translations.literal: Shangzhi was very quick-witted; at the time the people wished to build a temple for Emperor Xiaowu and were uncertain what to name it.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi was exceptionally quick-witted; when the people wished to erect a temple to Emperor Xiaowu, they were unsure what to call it.

sentences.zh: 尚之應聲曰：「宜名天保。

translations.literal: Shangzhi answered on the spot, "It should be named Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi answered at once, "Call it Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 詩云：'天保，下報上也。

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'Tianbao—below repays what is above.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, 'Tianbao—the lower repays the higher.

sentences.zh: '」時服其機速。

translations.literal: At the time all admired his quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone at court admired his ready wit.

sentences.zh: 廢帝年已漸長，凶志轉成，欲有所為，法興每相禁制。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor was gradually growing older, his vicious intent taking shape; when he wished to act, Faxing always restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: As the Deposed Emperor grew older, his cruel impulses hardened; whenever he meant to act, Faxing held him back.

sentences.zh: 謂帝曰：「官所為如此，欲作營陽邪？」

translations.literal: He told the emperor, "Your Majesty acts in this way—do you wish to become another Prince of Yingyang?
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor, "If Your Majesty goes on like this, do you mean to end as another Prince of Yingyang?

sentences.zh: 帝意稍不能平。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind grew somewhat unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's resentment began to stir.

sentences.zh: 所愛幸閹人華願兒有盛寵，賜與金帛無算。

translations.literal: The eunuch Huayuan'er, whom he favored, enjoyed extravagant favor; gifts of gold and silk to him were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The favored eunuch Huayuan'er enjoyed boundless favor; gold and silk poured upon him without measure.

sentences.zh: 法興常加裁減，願兒甚恨之。

translations.literal: Faxing often cut back his grants, and Huayuan'er hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing kept trimming his rewards, and Huayuan'er came to hate him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗使願兒出入市里，察聽風謠，而道路之言，謂法興為真天子，帝為贗天子。

translations.literal: The emperor once sent Huayuan'er into the markets to listen to popular songs, and on the roads people said that Faxing was the true Son of Heaven and the emperor a counterfeit Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sent Huayuan'er into the streets to hear what people were singing, and rumor had it that Faxing was the real emperor and the throne a counterfeit.

sentences.zh: 願兒因此告帝曰：「外間雲宮中有兩天子，官是一人，戴法興是一人。

translations.literal: Huayuan'er therefore reported to the emperor, "Outside they say there are two Sons of Heaven in the palace—Your Majesty is one, and Dai Faxing is one.
translations.idiomatic: Huayuan'er then told the emperor, "People outside say there are two emperors in the palace—Your Majesty is one, and Dai Faxing is the other.

sentences.zh: 官在深宮中，人物不相接，法興與太宰、顏、柳一體，往來門客恒有數百，內外士庶無不畏服之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty dwells deep in the inner palace and has no contact with people; Faxing is one body with the Grand Tutor and Yan and Liu—the clients who come and go at his gate are always in the hundreds, and gentlemen and commoners inside and outside all fear and submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty lives deep within the palace and never meets the world; Faxing moves as one with the Grand Tutor and with Yan and Liu—hundreds of clients pass his gate, and none inside or outside the court dares defy him.

sentences.zh: 法興是孝武左右，復久在宮闈，今將他人作一家，深恐此坐席非復官許。」

translations.literal: Faxing was at Emperor Xiaowu's side and has long been in the women's quarters; now he is making a household of others—I deeply fear this seat will no longer be permitted to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing stood at Emperor Xiaowu's elbow and has spent years in the inner palace; now he is building a faction of his own—I fear Your Majesty's throne may no longer be yours alone.

sentences.zh: 帝遂免法興官，徙付遠郡，尋於家賜死。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon removed Faxing from office, banished him to a distant commandery, and soon had him granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then stripped Faxing of office, sent him to a distant commandery, and soon ordered him to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 法興臨死，封閉庫藏，使家人謹錄鑰牡。

translations.literal: As Faxing faced death he sealed his storehouses and had his family carefully record the keys.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, Faxing sealed his treasuries and had his household carefully inventory every key.

sentences.zh: 死一宿，又殺其二子，截法興棺兩和，籍沒財物。

translations.literal: One night after his death they killed his two sons as well, split the two panels of Faxing's coffin, and confiscated his property.
translations.idiomatic: A night after his death his two sons were killed too, his coffin panels were split apart, and his property was seized.

sentences.zh: 法興能為文章，頗行於世。

translations.literal: Faxing could compose literary works, which circulated fairly widely in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing wrote essays that enjoyed a fair circulation in his day.

sentences.zh: 死後，帝敕巢尚之曰：「不謂法興積釁累愆，遂至於此。

translations.literal: After his death the emperor ordered Chao Shangzhi, saying, "I did not expect that Faxing's accumulated offenses and repeated faults would come to this.
translations.idiomatic: After Faxing's death the emperor addressed Chao Shangzhi: "I never thought Faxing's piled-up crimes would end like this.

sentences.zh: 吾今自覽萬機，卿等宜竭誠盡力。」

translations.literal: I shall now personally review all affairs of state; you should devote your loyalty and utmost effort.
translations.idiomatic: I will now govern in person; you must serve with full loyalty and effort.

sentences.zh: 尚之時為新安王子鸞撫軍中兵參軍、淮陵太守，乃解舍人，轉為撫軍諮議參軍，太守如故。

translations.literal: Shangzhi was then army staff officer on the staff of Prince Xin'an Ziluan's pacification army and governor of Huailing; he resigned as palace secretary and became advisory staff officer on the pacification army, retaining his governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi was then on Prince Xin'an Ziluan's staff as army officer and governor of Huailing; he gave up the secretary post for an advisory staff appointment while keeping the governorship.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，復以尚之兼中書通事舍人、南清河太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign Shangzhi was again made concurrently palace secretary for communications and governor of Southern Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Ming's reign Shangzhi again served concurrently as communications secretary and governor of Southern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 累遷黃門侍郎，出為新安太守，病卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to gentleman attendant at the palace gates, then sent out as governor of Xin'an, and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to gentleman attendant at the palace gates, was posted as governor of Xin'an, and died in office of illness.

sentences.zh: 戴明寶

translations.literal: Dai Mingbao
translations.idiomatic: Dai Mingbao

sentences.zh: 戴明寶，南東海丹徒人，亦歷員外散騎侍郎、給事中。

translations.literal: Dai Mingbao was a native of Dantu in Southern Donghai and also served as supernumerary attendant cavalier and palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Mingbao came from Dantu in Southern Donghai and had served as supernumerary attendant cavalier and as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝武時，帶南清河太守。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu he held the concurrent post of governor of Southern Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu he concurrently governed Southern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，權任悉歸法興，而明寶輕矣。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, all power and trust went to Faxing, and Mingbao was slighted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor acceded, power passed entirely to Faxing, and Mingbao's standing fell.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，天下反叛，以明寶舊人，屢經戎事，復委任之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign the realm rebelled; because Mingbao was an old associate who had repeatedly seen military service, he was again entrusted with office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne amid widespread rebellion, Mingbao—an old confidant with long military experience—was entrusted once more.

sentences.zh: 後坐納貨賄系尚方，尋被宥。

translations.literal: Later he was imprisoned in the imperial workshops for accepting bribes, but was soon pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was later imprisoned in the imperial workshops for bribery, then soon pardoned.

sentences.zh: 位宣城太守。

translations.literal: He reached the post of governor of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to governor of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 升明初，年老，拜太中大夫，病卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengming he was old and was appointed grand master of the palace, then died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shengming era, in his old age, he was made grand master of the palace and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 武陵國典書令董元嗣與法興、明寶等俱為孝武南中郎典簽，元嘉三十年，奉使還都，會元凶弑立，遣元嗣南還，報上以徐湛之等反。

translations.literal: Dong Yuansi, director of documents of Wuling kingdom, had together with Faxing, Mingbao, and the rest served as registry clerks on Emperor Xiaowu's staff as commander of the Southern Gentlemen; in the thirtieth year of Yuanjia, while on a mission returning to the capital, he encountered the crown prince's regicide and accession; the prince sent Yuansi back south to report to the emperor that Xu Tanzhi and others had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yuansi, director of documents for Wuling, had served with Faxing and Mingbao as registry clerks on Emperor Xiaowu's southern staff; in the thirtieth year of Yuanjia, returning to the capital on mission, he found the crown prince had murdered his father and seized the throne; the prince sent Yuansi south again to tell the emperor that Xu Tanzhi and others were in revolt.

sentences.zh: 上時在巴口，元嗣具言弑狀。

translations.literal: The emperor was then at Bakou; Yuansi gave a full account of the regicide.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Bakou, and Yuansi described the murder in full.

sentences.zh: 上遣元嗣下都奉表於劭，既而上舉義兵，劭詔責元嗣，元嗣答云：「始下未有反謀。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent Yuansi down to the capital to present a memorial to Shao; afterward the emperor raised righteous troops, and Shao issued an edict rebuking Yuansi; Yuansi replied, "When I first went down there was no plan to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yuansi to the capital with a memorial for Shao; when the emperor rose in arms, Shao rebuked Yuansi by edict, and Yuansi answered, "When I first went to the capital there was no thought of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 劭不信，備加考掠，不服遂死。

translations.literal: Shao did not believe him, tortured him to the full, and when he would not confess, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shao refused to believe him, tortured him severely, and when he would not yield, had him killed.

sentences.zh: 孝武事克，贈員外散騎侍郎，使文士蘇寶生為之誄焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu's cause prevailed, Yuansi was posthumously given the rank of supernumerary attendant cavalier, and the literary man Su Baosheng was commissioned to compose his eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu's victory, Yuansi was posthumously made supernumerary attendant cavalier, and the scholar Su Baosheng was asked to write his funeral elegy.

sentences.zh: 大明中，又有奚顯度者，南東海郯人，官至員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Daming era there was also Xi Xiandu, a native of Tan in Southern Donghai, who reached the post of supernumerary attendant cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daming era there was also Xi Xiandu of Tan in Southern Donghai, who rose to supernumerary attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 孝武嘗使主領人功，而苛虐無道，動加捶撲，暑雨寒雪，不聽暫休，人不堪命，或自經死。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu once had him supervise corvée labor; he was harsh and cruel beyond measure, constantly beating people; in summer heat, rain, or winter snow he allowed no rest, and people could not bear it—some hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu put him in charge of corvée labor; he was savagely cruel, beating workers constantly and allowing no pause in heat, rain, or snow—some hanged themselves to escape.

sentences.zh: 時建康縣考囚，或用方材壓額及踝脛，人間謠曰：「甯得建康壓額，不能受奚度拍。」

translations.literal: At the time when Jiankang county examined prisoners they sometimes pressed square timbers on the forehead and ankles; among the people a song ran, "Better the Jiankang press on the brow than a beating from Xi Du.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang county tortured prisoners they sometimes pressed square beams on forehead and ankles; folk sang, "Better Jiankang's press on the brow than a blow from Xi Du.

sentences.zh: 又相戲曰：「勿反顧，付奚度。」

translations.literal: They also joked among themselves, "Do not look back—hand him over to Xi Du."
translations.idiomatic: People also joked, "Don't look back—or you'll be handed to Xi Du."

sentences.zh: 其酷暴如此。

translations.literal: Such was his cruelty and violence.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the measure of his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝嘗戲云：「顯度刻虐為百姓疾，比當除之。」

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor once jested, saying, "Xiandu's harsh cruelty is a scourge to the people; he should be removed before long.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Deposed Emperor once joked, "Xiandu's cruelty is the people's plague—he ought to be removed soon.

sentences.zh: 左右因唱「爾」，即日宣殺焉。

translations.literal: His attendants thereupon chanted "Execute," and that same day the order to kill was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants took up the chant "Execute," and that very day Xiandu was put to death.

sentences.zh: 時人比之孫皓殺岑昏。

translations.literal: People of the time compared this to Sun Hao's killing of Cen Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries compared it to Sun Hao's execution of Cen Hun.

sentences.zh: 徐爰，字長玉，南琅邪開陽人也。

translations.literal: Xu Ai, style name Changyu, was a native of Kaiyang in Southern Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ai, styled Changyu, came from Kaiyang in Southern Langye.

sentences.zh: 本名瑗，後以與傅亮父同名，亮啟改為爰。

translations.literal: His original name was Yuan; later, because it was the same as Fu Liang's father's name, Liang memorialized to have it changed to Ai.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally named Yuan; because this matched the name of Fu Liang's father, Liang petitioned to have it changed to Ai.

sentences.zh: 初為晉琅邪王大司馬府中典軍，從北征，微密有意理，為武帝所知。

translations.literal: He first served as barracks officer in the great marshal's staff of Prince Langye of Jin; on the northern campaign he showed subtle understanding and sound judgment and came to Emperor Wu's notice.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as barracks officer on Prince Langye of Jin's staff; on the northern campaign his shrewd judgment won Emperor Wu's notice.

sentences.zh: 少帝在東宮，入侍左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shao was in the Eastern Palace he entered to attend at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shao was crown prince, Ai entered service at his side.

sentences.zh: 文帝初，又見親任，遂至殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen's reign he was again treated with personal trust and rose to palace attendant investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Wen's reign he again won personal favor and rose to palace investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年，轉南台御史，始興王浚後軍行參軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to censor of the southern bureau and became acting staff officer on the rear army of Prince Shixing Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he became a southern bureau censor and acting staff officer on Prince Shixing Jun's rear army.

sentences.zh: 復侍太子于東宮，遷員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He again attended the crown prince in the Eastern Palace and was promoted to supernumerary attendant cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: He again served the crown prince in the Eastern Palace and was promoted to supernumerary attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 文帝每出軍，常懸授兵略。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Wen took the field he would often entrust Ai with military plans in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Wen campaigned, he often gave Ai his battle plans in advance.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，重遣王玄謨等北侵，配爰五百人，隨軍碻磝，銜中旨臨時宣示。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he again sent Wang Xuanmo and others north on campaign, assigning Ai five hundred men to follow the army to Quepo, bearing the emperor's secret intent to proclaim on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: the twenty-ninth year of In he again sent Wang Xuanmo north; Ai was given five hundred men to accompany the army to Quepo and proclaim the emperor's secret orders as events unfolded.

sentences.zh: 孝武至新亭，江夏王義恭南奔，爰時在殿內，詐劭追義恭，因即得南走。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, Prince Jiangxia Yigong fled south; Ai was then inside the hall and pretended that Shao was pursuing Yigong, thus managing to flee south himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting and Prince Jiangxia Yigong fled south, Ai was in the hall; pretending Shao was pursuing Yigong, he slipped away south as well.

sentences.zh: 時孝武將即大位，軍府造次，不曉朝章，爰素諳其事，及至，莫不喜悅，以兼太常丞撰立儀注。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowu was about to take the great throne; the army headquarters was in disarray and did not understand court regulations—Ai had long been versed in such matters, and when he arrived everyone was delighted; he was made concurrently vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to draft the ritual protocols for accession.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Xiaowu prepared to ascend the throne, the military headquarters was in chaos and knew nothing of court ritual—Ai, who knew these matters thoroughly, was welcomed with relief and made vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to draft the accession ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 後兼尚書右丞，遷左丞。

translations.literal: Later he was concurrently right vice-director of the Secretariat and was promoted to left vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: He later served concurrently as right vice-director of the Secretariat and was promoted to left vice-director.

sentences.zh: 孝武崩，營景寧陵，以本官兼將作大匠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Ai oversaw construction of the Jingning tomb and was made concurrently director of palace construction while retaining his original post.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Ai supervised the Jingning mausoleum and was made concurrently director of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 爰便僻善事人，能得人主微旨，頗涉書傳，尤悉朝儀。

translations.literal: Ai was adroit and skilled at pleasing others; he could grasp the ruler's subtle intent; he had dipped into books and records and especially understood court ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Ai was clever at ingratiating himself, caught the ruler's unspoken wishes, had read widely, and knew court ritual better than anyone.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，便入侍左右，預參顧問。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia he entered to attend at the ruler's side and took part in consultation.
translations.idiomatic: From the opening years of Yuanjia he served at the ruler's side and joined in counsel.

sentences.zh: 長於附會，又飾以典文，故為文帝所任遇。

translations.literal: He excelled at accommodating himself to others, and further adorned this with classical learning; therefore he was entrusted and favored by Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at currying favor and wrapping it in scholarly display, he won Emperor Wen's trust and advancement.

sentences.zh: 大明世，委寄尤重，朝廷大禮儀，非爰議不行。

translations.literal: During the Daming era, the trust placed in him was especially heavy; for major court ceremonies and rituals, nothing proceeded without Ai's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Daming reign his authority grew even weightier: no major state ritual could proceed unless Xu Ai had weighed in on it.

sentences.zh: 雖復當時碩學所解過之者，既不敢立異議，所言亦不見從。

translations.literal: Even though some eminent scholars of the time surpassed him in learning, they neither dared raise opposing views, nor were their own statements adopted when they spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Even leading scholars who knew more than he did neither dared openly dissent, nor found their counsel heeded when they offered it.

sentences.zh: 孝武崩，公除後，晉安王子勳侍讀博士諮爰宜習業與不？

translations.literal: After Emperor Xiaowu died, once the period of official mourning had ended, the tutor-doctor serving Prince Jin'an Zixun asked Ai whether studying was permissible.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu's death and the end of the official mourning period, the tutor assigned to Prince Jin'an, Liu Zixun, asked Xu Ai whether the prince might resume his studies.

sentences.zh: 爰答曰：「居喪讀喪禮，習業何嫌。」

translations.literal: Ai replied, "While in mourning one reads the rites of mourning—what objection is there to continuing one's studies?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ai answered, "In mourning one reads the mourning rites—what harm is there in pursuing one's studies?

sentences.zh: 少日，始安王子真博士諮爰，爰曰：「小功廢業，三年喪何容讀書。」

translations.literal: A few days later, the tutor of Prince Shi'an Zizhen consulted Ai; Ai said, "For lesser mourning one abandons studies—how could reading books be allowed during three-year mourning?"
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the tutor to Prince Shi'an, Liu Zizhen, asked him the same question. Xu Ai said, "Lesser mourning suspends study—how could one read books during three-year mourning?"

sentences.zh: 其專斷乖謬皆如此。

translations.literal: His arbitrary decisions and perverse errors were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: His capricious and contradictory rulings were all of this sort.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝凶暴無道，殿省舊人多見罪黜，唯爰巧於將迎，始終無忤。

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor was fierce and tyrannical; many long-serving officials of the palace were punished and dismissed, but Ai alone was clever at ingratiating himself and never gave offense from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Deposed Emperor was violent and lawless; veteran palace officials were punished and removed in droves, yet Xu Ai alone knew how to flatter and please, and never once gave offense.

sentences.zh: 誅群公後，以爰為黃門侍郎，領射聲校尉，著作如故，封吳平縣子。

translations.literal: After the execution of the great officials, Ai was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently Commander of the She Sheng Guard, retaining his post as Director of Composition, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wuping County.
translations.idiomatic: After the purge of the senior ministers, he was made Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrent Commander of the She Sheng Guard, kept his post in the Composition Office, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wuping.

sentences.zh: 寵待隆密，群臣莫二。

translations.literal: Favor and treatment were lofty and intimate; among the ministers none was second.
translations.idiomatic: His favor was second to none among the entire court.

sentences.zh: 帝每出行，常與沈慶之、山陰公主同輦，爰亦預焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went out, he often shared a carriage with Shen Qingzhi and the Princess of Shanyin, and Ai also took part.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went abroad, he commonly rode in the same carriage with Shen Qingzhi and the Princess of Shanyin—and Xu Ai was included as well.

sentences.zh: 爰子希秀，甚有學解，亦閑篆隸，正覺、禪靈二寺碑，即希秀書也。

translations.literal: Ai's son Xixiu was greatly learned and perceptive, and also skilled in seal and clerical script; the stele inscriptions of the Zhengjue and Chanling temples were written by Xixiu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's son Xixiu was deeply learned and skilled in seal and clerical script; the steles at the Zhengjue and Chanling temples were his work.

sentences.zh: 爰之徙交州，明帝召希秀謂曰：「比當令卿父還。」

translations.literal: When Ai was banished to Jiaozhou, Emperor Ming summoned Xixiu and said, "Soon I shall have your father returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Ai was exiled to Jiaozhou, Emperor Ming summoned Xixiu and said, "I shall soon have your father brought back.

sentences.zh: 希秀再拜答曰：「臣父年老，恐不及後恩。」

translations.literal: Xixiu bowed twice and replied, "My father is old; I fear he may not survive to receive later kindness."
translations.idiomatic: Xixiu bowed twice and answered, "My father is aged; I fear he may not live to enjoy your grace much longer."

sentences.zh: 帝大嗟賞，即召爰還。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly admired this and immediately recalled Ai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and at once recalled Xu Ai.

sentences.zh: 希秀位驍騎將軍、淮南太守。

translations.literal: Xixiu rose to General of Majestic Cavalry and Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Xixiu rose to serve as General of Majestic Cavalry and Administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 子泓甚閑吏職，而在事刻薄，於人少恩。

translations.literal: His son Hong was very adept at official duties, yet in conduct was harsh and granted little kindness to others.
translations.idiomatic: Another son, Hong, was highly competent in office, but harsh in practice and sparing of kindness toward others.

sentences.zh: 仕齊歷位台郎，秣陵、建康令，湘東太守。

translations.literal: Serving in Qi he held in succession the posts of Secretariat Gentleman, Magistrate of Molin and Jiankang, and Administrator of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi he served successively as a Secretariat officer, magistrate of Molin and Jiankang, and administrator of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 阮佃夫

translations.literal: Ruan Dianfu
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Dianfu

sentences.zh: 阮佃夫，會稽諸暨人也。

translations.literal: Ruan Dianfu was a native of Zhuji in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Dianfu was a native of Zhuji in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 明帝初出合，選為主衣，後又請為世子師，甚見信待。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming first left the inner quarters, Dianfu was selected as Master of Garments; later he also requested to become tutor to the heir, and was greatly trusted and favored.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Ming first left the inner palace, Ruan was chosen as Master of Garments; he later asked to serve as tutor to the heir and won deep trust.

sentences.zh: 景和末，明帝被拘於殿內，住在秘書省，為帝所疑，大禍將至。

translations.literal: At the end of Jinghe, Emperor Ming was detained within the palace, residing in the Secretariat, suspected by the emperor; great calamity was about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jinghe reign, Emperor Ming was confined within the palace in the Secretariat office, viewed with suspicion by the emperor—a deadly crisis was imminent.

sentences.zh: 佃夫與王道隆、李道兒及帝左右琅邪淳于文祖謀共廢立。

translations.literal: Dianfu joined with Wang Daolong, Li Dao'er, and Chunyu Wenzi of Langya, a close attendant of the emperor, to plot together to depose and establish.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan joined Wang Daolong, Li Dao'er, and the emperor's attendant Chunyu Wenzi of Langya in a plot to depose the ruler and install another.

sentences.zh: 時直閣將軍柳光世亦與帝左右蘭陵繆方盛、丹陽周登之有密謀，未知所奉。

translations.literal: At the time General of Direct Guard Liu Guangshi also had a secret plot with the emperor's attendants Miao Fangsheng of Lanling and Zhou Dengzhi of Danyang, not yet knowing whom they would support.
translations.idiomatic: General of Direct Guard Liu Guangshi was also plotting secretly with the emperor's attendants Miao Fangsheng of Lanling and Zhou Dengzhi of Danyang, though they had not yet settled on a candidate.

sentences.zh: 登之與明帝有舊，方盛等乃使登之結佃夫，佃夫大悅。

translations.literal: Dengzhi had old ties with Emperor Ming; Fangsheng and the others therefore had Dengzhi win over Dianfu, and Dianfu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had old ties with Emperor Ming, so Miao and the others sent him to approach Ruan, who was delighted.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝立皇后，普暫撤諸王奄人，明帝左右錢藍生亦在例，事畢未被遣，密使藍生候帝。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor established the empress, all eunuchs of the various princes were temporarily withdrawn; Qian Lansheng among Emperor Ming's attendants was also within this measure. When the affair was concluded he was not sent away, and secretly they had Lansheng watch the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor installed his empress, eunuchs attached to the various princes were temporarily withdrawn—including Qian Lansheng, an attendant of Emperor Ming. Though the ceremony ended, Qian was not dismissed, and the conspirators secretly set him to watch the emperor.

sentences.zh: 慮事泄，藍生不欲自出，帝動止輒以告淳于文祖，令報佃夫。

translations.literal: Fearing that matters might leak, Lansheng did not wish to reveal himself; the emperor's every movement and halt he reported to Chunyu Wenzi, who was told to inform Dianfu.
translations.idiomatic: To keep the plot from leaking, Qian stayed out of sight; he reported the emperor's every move to Chunyu Wenzi, who relayed it to Ruan.

sentences.zh: 景和元年十一月二十九日晡時，帝出華林園。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month in the first year of Jinghe, at the third watch of the day, the emperor went out to Hualin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month of the first year of Jinghe, in the late afternoon, the emperor went out to Hualin Garden.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁、山陽王休佑、山陰主並侍側，明帝猶在秘書省不被召，益懼。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren, Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou, and the Princess of Shanyin all attended at his side; Emperor Ming remained in the Secretariat and was not summoned, growing ever more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian'an Xiuren, Prince Shanyang Xiuyou, and the Princess of Shanyin attended at his side, while Emperor Ming still languished uncalled in the Secretariat—his fear mounting.

sentences.zh: 佃夫以告外監典事東陽朱幼，又告主衣吳興壽寂之、細鎧主南彭城薑產之。

translations.literal: Dianfu told External Supervisor Commissioner Zhu You of Dongyang, and also told Master of Garments Shou Jizhi of Wuxing and Master of Light Armor Jiang Chanzhi of Nan Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan informed External Supervisor Commissioner Zhu You of Dongyang, Master of Garments Shou Jizhi of Wuxing, and Master of Light Armor Jiang Chanzhi of South Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 產之又語所領細鎧將臨淮王敬則，幼又告中書舍人戴明寶，並回應。

translations.literal: Chanzhi also spoke to the light-armor officer under his command Wang Jingze of Linhuai; You also told Secretariat Gentleman Dai Mingbao—and all responded in agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang also told the light-armor officer under his command, Wang Jingze of Linhuai; Zhu informed Secretariat Gentleman Dai Mingbao—and all pledged their support.

sentences.zh: 明寶、幼欲取其日向曉，佃夫等勸取開門鼓後。

translations.literal: Mingbao and You wished to act at daybreak on that day; Dianfu and the others urged acting after the drum signaling the opening of the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Dai and Zhu wanted to strike at daybreak, but Ruan and the others urged waiting until after the drum that opened the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 幼預約勒內外，使錢藍生密報建安王休仁等。

translations.literal: You beforehand arranged and constrained inner and outer units, and had Qian Lansheng secretly report to Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu coordinated forces inside and outside the palace and had Qian Lansheng secretly alert Prince Jian'an Xiuren and the others.

sentences.zh: 時帝欲南巡，腹心直閣將軍宗越等，其夕並聽出外裝束，唯有隊主樊僧整防華林閣，是柳光世鄉人。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor wished to tour the south; his trusted General of Direct Guard Zong Yue and others were all that evening permitted to go out to prepare their gear; only squad leader Fan Zhengzheng guarded Hualin Pavilion—he was a fellow townsman of Liu Guangshi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned a southern tour; his trusted general Zong Yue and others were allowed out that evening to prepare, leaving only squad leader Fan Zhengzheng to guard Hualin Pavilion—a townsman of Liu Guangshi.

sentences.zh: 光世要之，即受命。

translations.literal: Guangshi won him over, and he at once accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Liu won him over, and Fan immediately joined the plot.

sentences.zh: 姜產之又要隊副陽平聶慶及所領壯士會稽富靈符、吳郡俞道龍、丹陽宋逵之、陽平田嗣，並聚于慶省。

translations.literal: Jiang Chanzhi also won over squad deputy Nie Qing of Yangping and the stalwart soldiers under his command: Fu Lingfu of Kuaiji, Yu Daolong of Wu commandery, Song Kuizhi of Danyang, and Tian Si of Yangping—all gathered at Qing's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang also recruited squad deputy Nie Qing of Yangping and his men—Fu Lingfu of Kuaiji, Yu Daolong of Wu, Song Kuizhi of Danyang, and Tian Si of Yangping—who all assembled at Nie Qing's quarters.

sentences.zh: 佃夫慮力少，更欲招合，壽寂之曰：「謀廣或泄，不煩多人。」

translations.literal: Dianfu feared their force was too small and wished to recruit further; Shou Jizhi said, "If the plot grows broad it may leak—there is no need for many men.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan worried their numbers were too few and wanted more recruits, but Shou Jizhi said, "The wider the conspiracy, the more likely it leaks—we don't need many men.

sentences.zh: 時巫覡言後堂有鬼，其夕帝于竹林堂前與巫共射之，建安王休仁等、山陰主並從。

translations.literal: At the time shamans and diviners said there was a ghost in the rear hall; that evening the emperor, before Zhulin Hall, shot at it together with the shamans; Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and the others and the Princess of Shanyin all followed.
translations.idiomatic: Shamans had reported a ghost in the rear hall; that evening the emperor went before Zhulin Hall to shoot at it with them, accompanied by Prince Jian'an Xiuren and the Princess of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 帝素不悅寂之，見輒切齒。

translations.literal: The emperor had never liked Jizhi; whenever he saw him he ground his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long disliked Shou Jizhi and would grind his teeth at the sight of him.

sentences.zh: 寂之既與佃夫等成謀，又慮禍至，抽刀前入，薑產之隨其後，淳于文祖、繆方盛、周登之、富靈符、聶慶、田嗣、王敬則、俞道龍、宋逵之又繼進。

translations.literal: Jizhi, having already formed the plot with Dianfu and the others and fearing calamity would arrive, drew his sword and entered first; Jiang Chanzhi followed behind him; Chunyu Wenzi, Miao Fangsheng, Zhou Dengzhi, Fu Lingfu, Nie Qing, Tian Si, Wang Jingze, Yu Daolong, and Song Kuizhi advanced in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Having already pledged himself to the plot and fearing discovery, Shou Jizhi drew his sword and rushed forward; Jiang Chanzhi followed, and Chunyu Wenzi, Miao Fangsheng, Zhou Dengzhi, Fu Lingfu, Nie Qing, Tian Si, Wang Jingze, Yu Daolong, and Song Kuizhi piled in after them.

sentences.zh: 休仁聞行聲甚疾，謂休佑曰：「作矣。」

translations.literal: Xiuren, hearing footsteps very swift, said to Xiuyou, "It is done.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren heard rapid footsteps and said to Xiuyou, "It has begun.

sentences.zh: 相隨奔景陽山。

translations.literal: They followed one another in flight to Jingyang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Together they fled to Jingyang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 帝見寂之至，引弓射之，不中，乃走。

translations.literal: The emperor, seeing Jizhi arrive, drew his bow and shot at him but missed, then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Shou Jizhi approach, the emperor strung his bow and shot at him, missed, and ran.

sentences.zh: 寂之追殺之。

translations.literal: Jizhi pursued and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Jizhi chased him down and killed him.

sentences.zh: 事定，宣令宿衛曰：「湘東王受太后令除狂主，今已太平。」

translations.literal: Once the affair was settled, they proclaimed to the night guard, "The Prince of Xiangdong, receiving the empress dowager's order to remove the mad ruler, has now restored peace."
translations.idiomatic: When the deed was done, they announced to the palace guard: "The Prince of Xiangdong, acting on the empress dowager's order, has removed the mad emperor—order is restored."

sentences.zh: 薛索兒度淮為寇，山陽太守程天祚又反，佃夫與諸軍破薛索兒，降天祚。

translations.literal: Xue Suo'er crossed the Huai to plunder as a rebel; the Administrator of Shanyang Cheng Tianzuo also rebelled. Dianfu with the various armies defeated Xue Suo'er and accepted Tianzuo's surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Suo'er crossed the Huai to raid and Shanyang administrator Cheng Tianzuo rebelled, Ruan joined the armies that crushed Xue and accepted Cheng's surrender.

sentences.zh: 後轉太子步兵校尉、南魯郡太守，侍太子于東宮。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Commandant of Footsoldiers of the Heir Apparent and Administrator of Nanlu commandery, attending the heir in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Commandant of Footsoldiers of the Heir Apparent and administrator of Nanlu commandery, attending the crown prince in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年，以本官兼遊擊將軍，及輔國將軍孟次陽與二衛參員直。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi, with his existing office he concurrently served as General of Mobile Cavalry, and together with General Who Supports the State Meng Ciyang joined the two Guards on rotating palace duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taishi he was made concurrent General of Mobile Cavalry and, with General Who Supports the State Meng Ciyang, shared rotating duty with the two palace guards.

sentences.zh: 次陽字崇基，平昌安丘人也，位冠軍將軍卒。

translations.literal: Ciyang, courtesy name Chongji, was a native of Anqiu in Pingchang; he reached General Who Vanquishes the Enemy and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Ciyang, style name Chongji, was from Anqiu in Pingchang commandery; he rose to General Who Vanquishes the Enemy and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 時佃夫及王道隆、楊運長並執權，亞於人主，巢、戴大明之世，方之蔑如也。

translations.literal: At the time Dianfu, Wang Daolong, and Yang Yunchang all held power, second only to the ruler; compared with Chao and Dai in the Daming era, they made those two seem negligible indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Dianfu, Wang Daolong, and Yang Yunchang then wielded power second only to the throne—making even Chao Yu and Dai Faxing of the Daming era look insignificant by comparison.

sentences.zh: 嘗正旦應合朔，尚書奏遷元會。

translations.literal: Once, on New Year's Day when the new moon coincided, the Secretariat memorialized to postpone the New Year assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when New Year's Day fell on the new moon, the Secretariat recommended postponing the New Year court assembly.

sentences.zh: 佃夫曰：「元正慶會，國之大禮，何不遷合朔日邪？」

translations.literal: Dianfu said, "The New Year's festive assembly is a great state ritual—why not move the day of the new moon instead?
translations.idiomatic: Ruan objected: "The New Year celebration is one of the state's greatest rites—why not reschedule the new-moon observance instead?

sentences.zh: 其不稽古如此。

translations.literal: His failure to consult antiquity was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his indifference to precedent.

sentences.zh: 大通貨賄，凡事非重賂不行。

translations.literal: He broadly trafficked in bribes; for anything, unless a heavy gift was given, it would not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: He traded openly in bribes; nothing got done without a hefty payment.

sentences.zh: 人有餉絹二百疋，嫌少不答書。

translations.literal: Someone presented two hundred bolts of silk as a gift; deeming it too little, he did not reply with a letter.
translations.idiomatic: When a petitioner sent two hundred bolts of silk, he considered the gift too small and did not even send a reply.

sentences.zh: 宅舍園池，諸王邸第莫及。

translations.literal: His residence, gardens, and ponds—no princely mansion could match them.
translations.idiomatic: His mansion, gardens, and ponds surpassed every princely estate.

sentences.zh: 女妓數十，藝貌冠絕當時。

translations.literal: He had several tens of female performers; in skill and beauty they topped the age.
translations.idiomatic: He kept dozens of courtesans whose talent and beauty were unmatched in the realm.

sentences.zh: 金玉錦繡之飾，宮掖不逮也。

translations.literal: Even the palace women's ornaments in gold, jade, brocades, and embroidery could not compare.
translations.idiomatic: Even the palace women's gold, jade, brocade, and embroidery paled beside his finery.

sentences.zh: 每制一衣，造一物，都下莫不法效焉。

translations.literal: Whenever he made a garment or crafted an object, none in the capital did not take it as a model to imitate.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever garment he designed or object he commissioned became the fashion throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 於宅內開瀆東出十許裏，塘岸整潔，泛輕舟，奏女樂。

translations.literal: Within his residence he opened a canal extending east for some ten li; its banks were neatly finished, and he floated light boats upon it with female musicians performing.
translations.idiomatic: He dug a canal from his estate eastward for some ten li, its banks immaculately maintained, where he floated light boats to the accompaniment of female musicians.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人劉休嘗詣之，遇佃夫出行，中路相逢，要休同反。

translations.literal: Secretariat Gentleman Liu Xiu once went to visit him; encountering Dianfu on an outing, they met midway on the road, and Dianfu invited Xiu to return together.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Gentleman Liu Xiu once came to call on him; they met on the road while Ruan was out, and Ruan invited Liu to turn back with him.

sentences.zh: 就席便命施設，一時珍羞，莫不畢備。

translations.literal: Once seated he immediately ordered things laid out; in an instant every delicacy was fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Once seated, he gave orders at once—and every delicacy appeared as if by magic.

sentences.zh: 凡諸火劑，並皆始熟，如此者數十種。

translations.literal: All the various hot dishes were each just finished cooking; there were dozens of such kinds.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of hot dishes, each freshly cooked, appeared together in this way.

sentences.zh: 佃夫常作數十人饌以待賓客，故造次便辦，類皆如此，雖晉世王、石不能過也。

translations.literal: Dianfu commonly prepared fare for several tens of people against the arrival of guests; hence in a sudden moment everything was ready—all like this; even the Wangs and Shis of the Jin age could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: He routinely kept food prepared for dozens of guests, so even on the spur of the moment a feast was ready—luxury that even the Wangs and Shis of Jin could not match.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，軍功既多，爵秩無序，佃夫僕從附隸皆受不次之位：捉車人武賁中郎將，傍馬者員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, as military merit was plentiful and ranks and titles were disorderly, Dianfu's servants and attendants who followed him all received extraordinary appointments: the man who held his carriage became a Chamberlain for Palace Attendants Central Gentleman; the man who walked beside his horse became an Attendant Outside Regular.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taishi years, with military honors proliferating and promotions in disarray, even Ruan's carriage attendants received extraordinary rank—a man who held his carriage might become a Chamberlain for Attendants Central Gentleman, and a groomsman an Outside Attendant.

sentences.zh: 朝士貴賤，莫不自結，而矜傲無所降意，入其室者唯吳興沈勃、吳郡張澹數人而已。

translations.literal: Court officials high and low all attached themselves to him of their own accord, yet he was proud and haughty, deferring to no one; those who entered his presence were only a few such as Shen Bo of Wuxing and Zhang Dan of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of every rank sought his favor, yet he condescended to none—only a handful, such as Shen Bo of Wuxing and Zhang Dan of Wu, were admitted into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 元徽三年，遷黃門侍郎，領右衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhui he was promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanhui he was promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrent General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，改領驍騎將軍，遷南豫州刺史、曆陽太守，猶管內任。

translations.literal: The following year he changed to concurrent General of Majestic Cavalry, was transferred to Inspector of South Yuzhou and Administrator of Liyang, yet still managed inner court duties.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became concurrent General of Majestic Cavalry and inspector of South Yuzhou and administrator of Liyang, while still retaining his palace duties.

sentences.zh: 時廢帝倡狂，好出遊走。

translations.literal: At the time the Deposed Emperor was wanton and frenzied, fond of going out to roam.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Deposed Emperor had turned wild and reckless, delighting in roaming abroad.

sentences.zh: 始出宮，猶整羽儀隊仗，俄而棄部伍，單騎與數人相隨，或出郊野，或入市廛，內外莫不憂懼。

translations.literal: When he first left the palace, he still arranged feathered insignia and escorts; presently he abandoned his ranks, riding alone with only several men following, sometimes going to the outskirts, sometimes entering marketplaces—inside and outside, none were not worried and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: At first he left the palace with full ceremonial guard; soon he abandoned his retinue and rode alone with only a few companions, ranging to the countryside or wandering through market streets—arousing dread throughout court and capital.

sentences.zh: 佃夫密與直合將軍申伯宗、步兵校尉朱幼、于天寶謀共廢帝，立安成王。

translations.literal: Dianfu secretly joined with General of Direct Guard Shen Bozong, Commandant of Footsoldiers Zhu You, and Yu Tianbao in a plot jointly to depose the emperor and establish the Prince of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan secretly plotted with General of Direct Guard Shen Bozong, Commandant of Footsoldiers Zhu You, and Yu Tianbao to depose the emperor and install the Prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 五年春，帝欲往江乘射雉。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, the emperor wished to go to Jiangcheng to shoot pheasants.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year, the emperor planned to go to Jiangcheng for pheasant hunting.

sentences.zh: 帝每出，常留隊仗在樂游苑前，棄之而去。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went out, he commonly left his escort at the front of Leyou Garden and abandoned them to go on.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went out, he habitually left his guard at Leyou Garden and rode off without them.

sentences.zh: 佃夫欲稱太后令喚隊仗還，閉城門，分人守石頭、東府，遣人執帝廢之，自為揚州刺史輔政。

translations.literal: Dianfu wished to claim an empress dowager's order to summon the escort back, close the city gates, divide men to guard Stone City and the Eastern Headquarters, send men to seize the emperor and depose him, and himself become Inspector of Yangzhou to assist in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan planned to invoke the empress dowager's authority to recall the guard, shut the city gates, garrison Stone City and the Eastern Headquarters, seize and depose the emperor, and install himself as inspector of Yangzhou to rule as regent.

sentences.zh: 與幼等已成謀，會帝不成向江乘，故事不行。

translations.literal: He and You and the others had already completed the plot, but as the emperor did not in the end go toward Jiangcheng, the affair could not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was ready, but the emperor never went to Jiangcheng after all, and the plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 于天寶因以其謀告帝，帝乃收佃夫、幼、伯宗于光祿外部賜死。

translations.literal: Yu Tianbao thereupon reported their plot to the emperor; the emperor then seized Dianfu, You, and Bozong and granted them death outside the Guanglu office.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tianbao betrayed the conspiracy to the emperor, who had Ruan, Zhu, and Shen arrested and executed just outside the Guanglu office.

sentences.zh: 佃夫、幼等罪止一身，其餘無所問。

translations.literal: The guilt of Dianfu, You, and the others stopped with their own persons; the rest were not investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ruan, Zhu, and their immediate co-conspirators were punished; no wider purge followed.

sentences.zh: 幼泰始初為外監配衣，諸軍征討，有濟辦之能，遂官陟三品，為奉朝請、南高平太守，封安浦縣侯。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Taishi, You served as external supervisor distributing garments; in the various armies' campaigns he had the ability to supply needs, and thus his office rose to the third rank: he became Court Attendant and Administrator of South Gaoping, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anpu County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu You had begun in Taishi as an external supervisor issuing uniforms; his talent for provisioning armies carried him to third rank as court attendant, administrator of South Gaoping, and Marquis of Anpu.

sentences.zh: 于天寶

translations.literal: Yu Tianbao
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tianbao

sentences.zh: 于天寶，其先胡人，豫竹林堂功，元徽中封鄂縣子。

translations.literal: Yu Tianbao—his ancestors were barbarians; he took part in the Zhulin Hall exploit; in Yuanhui he was enfeoffed as Viscount of E County.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tianbao's family was of non-Han origin; he had taken part in the killing at Zhulin Hall and was enfeoffed as Viscount of E during the Yuanhui era.

sentences.zh: 發佃夫謀，以為清河太守、右軍將軍。

translations.literal: For exposing Dianfu's plot he was made Administrator of Qinghe and General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: For betraying Ruan's conspiracy he was made administrator of Qinghe and General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 升明中，齊高帝以其反復賜死。

translations.literal: In the Shengming era, Emperor Gao of Qi because of his fickleness granted him death.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengming era, Emperor Gao of Qi had him executed for his treachery.

sentences.zh: 壽寂之位太子屯騎校尉、南泰山太守，多納貨賄，請謁無窮。

translations.literal: Shou Jizhi held the posts of Commandant of Cavalry in the Retinue of the Heir Apparent and Administrator of South Taishan; he accepted many bribes, and petitions and visits were endless.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Jizhi served as Commandant of Cavalry of the Heir Apparent and administrator of South Taishan, accepting endless bribes and entertaining ceaseless petitioners.

sentences.zh: 有一不從，便切齒罵詈，常云：「利刀在手，何憂不辦」。

translations.literal: If any request was not granted, he at once ground his teeth and reviled them, often saying, "With a sharp blade in hand, what worry is there that it cannot be done?"
translations.idiomatic: When anyone refused him, he would snarl curses and boast, "With a sharp blade in hand, what can I not accomplish?"

sentences.zh: 鞭尉吏，斫邏將，後為有司所奏，徙送越州。

translations.literal: He flogged gate officers and hacked at patrol commanders; later he was impeached by the relevant officials and was banished and sent to Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He beat gate officers and slashed at patrol captains, until impeachment sent him into exile in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 至豫章謀叛，乃殺之。

translations.literal: When he reached Yuzhang and plotted rebellion, they then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Yuzhang and plotted rebellion, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 姜產之位南濟陽太守。

translations.literal: Jiang Chanzhi held the post of Administrator of South Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Chanzhi served as administrator of South Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 後北侵魏，戰敗見殺。

translations.literal: Later he invaded Wei in the north, was defeated in battle, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He later led a northern campaign against Wei, was defeated, and killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 王道隆

translations.literal: Wang Daolong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daolong

sentences.zh: 王道隆，吳興烏程人。

translations.literal: Wang Daolong was a native of Wucheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daolong was a native of Wucheng in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 兄道迄涉學善書，形貌又美，吳興太守王韶之謂人曰：「有子弟如王道迄，無所少。」

translations.literal: His elder brother Daoqi was broadly learned and skilled at calligraphy, and his appearance was also handsome; the Administrator of Wuxing Wang Shaozhi said to others, "To have sons and younger brothers like Wang Daoqi—one lacks for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Wang Daoqi was erudite and an excellent calligrapher, handsome as well; Wuxing administrator Wang Shaozhi remarked, "With sons like Wang Daoqi, a man wants for nothing.

sentences.zh: 道隆亦知書，泰始二年，兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: Daolong also knew calligraphy; in the second year of Taishi he concurrently served as Secretariat Attendant for Current Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daolong was also literate; in the second year of Taishi he became concurrent Secretariat Attendant for Current Affairs.

sentences.zh: 道隆為明帝所委，過於佃夫，而和謹自保，不妄毀傷人。

translations.literal: Daolong was entrusted by Emperor Ming even more than Dianfu, yet he was harmonious and cautious in preserving himself and did not recklessly slander and harm people.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming relied on Wang even more than on Ruan, yet he remained moderate and cautious, never casually slandering others.

sentences.zh: 執權既久，家產豐積，豪麗雖不及佃夫，而精整過之。

translations.literal: Having held power for long, his household wealth was abundantly accumulated; though his lavish splendor did not match Dianfu's, his refinement and order surpassed it.
translations.idiomatic: Long in power, he amassed great wealth; though his ostentation fell short of Ruan's, his taste and orderliness exceeded it.

sentences.zh: 元徽二年，桂陽王休範舉兵，乃以討佃夫、道隆及楊運長為名。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui, Prince of Guiyang Xiufan raised troops, taking as his banner the campaign to destroy Dianfu, Daolong, and Yang Yunchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhui, Prince Guiyang Xiufan took up arms, claiming as his cause the overthrow of Ruan Dianfu, Wang Daolong, and Yang Yunchang.

sentences.zh: 休範奄至新亭見殺。

translations.literal: Xiufan suddenly arrived at Xinting and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan was killed when he suddenly reached Xinting.

sentences.zh: 楊運長

translations.literal: Yang Yunchang
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yunchang

sentences.zh: 紀僧真

translations.literal: Ji Sengzhen
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sengzhen

sentences.zh: 紀僧真，丹陽建康人也。

translations.literal: Ji Sengzhen was a native of Jiankang in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sengzhen was a native of Jiankang in Danyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 少隨逐征西將軍，蕭思話及子惠開，皆被賞遇。

translations.literal: In youth he followed and attended General Who Conquers the West Xiao Sihua and his son Xiao Huikai, and all were rewarded and favored.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served General Who Conquers the West Xiao Sihua and his son Xiao Huikai, winning favor from both.

sentences.zh: 惠開性苛，僧真以微過見罰，既而委任如舊。

translations.literal: Huikai was harsh by nature; Sengzhen was punished for a minor offense, yet afterward was entrusted as before.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai was harsh by nature. Sengzhen was once punished for a trifling fault, but afterward was entrusted with duties just as before.

sentences.zh: 及罷益州還都，不得志，而僧真事之愈謹。

translations.literal: When he was dismissed from Yizhou and returned to the capital, he was discouraged, yet Sengzhen served him all the more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: When Huikai was removed from Yizhou and returned to the capital, frustrated and out of favor, Sengzhen served him with even greater care.

sentences.zh: 惠開臨終歎曰：「紀僧真方當富貴，我不見也。」

translations.literal: On his deathbed Huikai sighed and said, "Ji Sengzhen is about to attain wealth and rank, but I shall not live to see it.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Huikai sighed and said, "Ji Sengzhen is on the verge of wealth and high office—but I shall not live to see it.

sentences.zh: 以僧真托劉彥節、周顒。

translations.literal: He entrusted Sengzhen to Liu Yanjie and Zhou Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted Sengzhen to Liu Yanjie and Zhou Yong.

sentences.zh: 初，惠開在益州，土反，被圍危急，有道人謂之曰：「城圍尋解，檀越貴門後方大興，無憂外賊也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huikai was in Yizhou, the local people rebelled and he was besieged in grave peril. A Daoist monk said to him, "The siege will soon be lifted; the noble house of the benefactor will flourish mightily hereafter—have no fear of outside enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Huikai was in Yizhou, the local people rose in revolt and he was besieged in dire peril. A Daoist monk told him, "The siege will soon be broken. Your noble house will rise to great eminence hereafter—have no fear of outside enemies.

sentences.zh: 惠開密謂僧真曰：「我子弟見在者並無異才，政是蕭道成耳。」

translations.literal: Huikai secretly told Sengzhen, "Among my sons and nephews now living, none has unusual talent—it is only Xiao Daocheng."
translations.idiomatic: Huikai secretly told Sengzhen, "Of my sons and nephews still living, none has exceptional talent. It will be Xiao Daocheng alone."

sentences.zh: 僧真憶其言，乃請事齊高帝，隨從在淮陰。

translations.literal: Sengzhen remembered his words and thereupon sought service under Emperor Gao of Qi, following him at Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen remembered these words and thereupon sought service under Emperor Gao of Qi, following him at Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 以閒書題，令答遠近書疏。

translations.literal: Because of his skill at informal calligraphy, he was set to reply to correspondence from near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at informal calligraphy, he was assigned to draft replies to correspondence from near and far.

sentences.zh: 自寒官曆至高帝冠軍府參軍主簿。

translations.literal: From a lowly post he rose through the ranks to become Staff Officer and Chief Clerk in Emperor Gao's Champion General headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: From humble office he rose step by step to Staff Officer and Chief Clerk in Emperor Gao's Champion General headquarters.

sentences.zh: 僧真夢蒿艾生滿江，驚而白之。

translations.literal: Sengzhen dreamed that wormwood and mugwort filled the entire river; startled, he reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen dreamed that wormwood and mugwort filled the whole river. Alarmed, he reported the dream.

sentences.zh: 高帝曰：「詩人采蕭，蕭即艾也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao said, "The poets gather xiao; xiao is mugwort.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said, "The poets gather xiao—and xiao is mugwort.

sentences.zh: 蕭生斷流，卿勿廣言。」

translations.literal: Xiao stops the flow—do not speak of this widely.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao blocks the current—do not spread this talk abroad.

sentences.zh: 其見親如此。

translations.literal: Such was the degree of his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the intimacy in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 後除南台御史、高帝領軍功曹。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Censor of the Southern Office and Merit Officer on Emperor Gao's staff as Director of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Censor of the Southern Office and Merit Officer on Emperor Gao's staff at the Directorate of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 上將廢立，謀之袁粲、褚彥回。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to depose and install a ruler, he consulted Yuan Can and Chu Yanhui.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne was about to change hands, Emperor Gao consulted Yuan Can and Chu Yanhui.

sentences.zh: 僧真啟上曰：「今朝廷倡狂，人不自保，天下之望，不在袁、褚，明公豈得默己，坐受夷滅？

translations.literal: Sengzhen addressed the emperor, saying, "Now the court is run wild and no one can protect himself. The hope of the realm does not rest with Yuan and Chu—how can Your Excellency keep silent and sit by to be wiped out?
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen addressed the emperor: "The court has gone mad, and no one can feel safe. The hopes of the realm do not rest with Yuan and Chu. How can Your Excellency hold your peace and sit waiting to be destroyed?

sentences.zh: 存亡之機，仰希熟慮。」

translations.literal: The moment of survival or destruction hangs on this—I beg you to consider it deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The choice between survival and ruin turns on this—I beg you to weigh it carefully.

sentences.zh: 高帝納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 高帝欲度廣陵起兵，僧真又曰：「主上雖復狂釁，而累代皇基，猶固磐石。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao wished to cross to Guangling and raise troops. Sengzhen again said, "Although the sovereign is indeed reckless and sinful, the imperial foundation built over generations remains firm as bedrock.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao planned to cross the Yangtze to Guangling and raise an army. Sengzhen again said, "Though the sovereign is indeed reckless and lawless, the imperial foundation built over generations still stands firm as bedrock.

sentences.zh: 今百口北度，何必得俱；

translations.literal: If the whole household crosses north now, must everyone succeed in crossing together?
translations.idiomatic: If the whole household crosses north now, can you be sure all will make it across together?

sentences.zh: 縱得廣陵城，天子居深宮，施號令，目明公為逆，何以避此？

translations.literal: Even if you take Guangling, the Son of Heaven will remain in the deep palace issuing edicts and branding Your Excellency a rebel—how will you escape that?
translations.idiomatic: Even if you take Guangling, the Son of Heaven will remain in the inner palace issuing orders and denouncing Your Excellency as a rebel—how will you escape that charge?

sentences.zh: 如其不勝，則應北走。

translations.literal: If you do not succeed, you must flee north.
translations.idiomatic: If you fail, you will have no choice but to flee north.

sentences.zh: 竊謂此非萬全策也。」

translations.literal: I submit that this is not a plan of complete security.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that this is no plan of complete safety.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿顧家，豈能逐我行邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You are thinking of your family—surely you cannot follow me in this, can you?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are thinking of your family—surely you cannot follow me in this?"

sentences.zh: 僧真頓首稱無貳。

translations.literal: Sengzhen prostrated himself and declared he had no divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen prostrated himself and declared that his loyalty was undivided.

sentences.zh: 升明元年，除員外郎，帶東武城令，尋除給事中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming he was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman, concurrently Magistrate of Dongwucheng, and soon made Attendant Within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengming he was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman and concurrent magistrate of Dongwucheng, and soon afterward was made Attendant Within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 高帝坐東府高樓望石頭城，僧真在側。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao sat in the high tower of the Eastern Residence looking toward Stone City; Sengzhen was at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao sat in the upper tower of the Eastern Residence gazing toward Stone City, with Sengzhen at his side.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「諸將勸我誅袁、劉，我意未願便爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The generals urge me to execute Yuan and Liu, but I am not yet willing to do so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The generals urge me to execute Yuan and Liu, but I am not yet willing to act so quickly.

sentences.zh: 及沈攸之事起，從高帝入朝堂。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's rebellion arose, he followed Emperor Gao into the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi's rebellion broke out, he followed Emperor Gao into the court hall.

sentences.zh: 石頭反夜，高帝遣眾軍掩討。

translations.literal: On the night Stone City rebelled, Emperor Gao dispatched armies to strike at them secretly.
translations.idiomatic: On the night Stone City rebelled, Emperor Gao sent troops to strike at the rebels by surprise.

sentences.zh: 宮城中望石頭火光及叫聲甚盛，人懷不測。

translations.literal: From the palace city they saw great fires and clamor at Stone City; people were filled with uncertainty.
translations.idiomatic: From the palace city they could see great fires blazing at Stone City and hear the uproar; everyone was filled with dread and uncertainty.

sentences.zh: 僧真謂眾曰：「叫聲不絕，是必官軍所攻。

translations.literal: Sengzhen told the crowd, "The cries do not cease—they must be the government troops attacking.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen told those around him, "The shouting has not stopped—that must mean the government troops are attacking.

sentences.zh: 火光起者，賊不容自燒其城，此必官軍勝也。」
