translations.literal: Where fires blaze, the rebels would not burn their own city—this must mean the government troops have won.
translations.idiomatic: Where the fires are rising, the rebels would not burn their own city—this must mean the government troops have won.

sentences.zh: 尋而啟石頭平。

translations.literal: Before long came word that Stone City had been pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Before long came word that Stone City had been pacified.

sentences.zh: 上出頓新亭，使僧真領千人在帳內。

translations.literal: The emperor went out to encamp at Xinting and had Sengzhen lead a thousand men inside the tent enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went out to encamp at Xinting and had Sengzhen command a thousand men within the tent enclosure.

sentences.zh: 初，上在領軍府，令僧真學上手跡下名，至是報答書疏皆付僧真。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was at the Directorate of Guards headquarters, he had Sengzhen learn to write in his hand and sign his name below; by now all letters of reply were entrusted to Sengzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the emperor was at the Directorate of the Guards, he had Sengzhen learn to imitate his handwriting and sign his name beneath it. By now all replies to correspondence were entrusted to Sengzhen.

sentences.zh: 上觀之笑曰：「我亦不復能別也。」

translations.literal: The emperor looked at them and laughed, "I could no longer tell them apart myself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked them over and laughed. "Even I could no longer tell them apart."

sentences.zh: 初，上在淮陰修理城，得古錫趺九枚，下有篆文，莫能識者。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was repairing the walls at Huaiyin, nine ancient tin pedestals were found, with seal script beneath that no one could read.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the emperor was repairing the walls at Huaiyin, nine ancient tin pedestals were unearthed, with seal script beneath them that no one could decipher.

sentences.zh: 僧真省事獨曰：「何須辯此文字，此自久遠之物。

translations.literal: Only Sengzhen, with his quick understanding, said, "Why bother to decipher these characters? These are obviously things of great antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Only Sengzhen, quick to grasp the point, said, "Why bother to decipher these characters? These are plainly objects of great antiquity.

sentences.zh: 錫而有九，九錫之征也。」

translations.literal: Tin, and there are nine of them—this is a portent of the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Tin—and nine of them. This is an omen of the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 高帝曰：「卿勿妄言。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gao said, "Do not speak rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said, "Do not speak rashly."

sentences.zh: 及上將拜齊公，已克日，有楊祖之謀於臨軒作難，僧真請上更選吉辰，尋而祖之事覺。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to be invested as Duke of Qi and the date was fixed, Yang Zuzhi plotted to create trouble at the ceremony in the hall; Sengzhen asked the emperor to choose another auspicious day, and soon Yang's plot was discovered.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to be invested as Duke of Qi and the date had been set, Yang Zuzhi plotted to raise trouble at the ceremony in the hall. Sengzhen asked the emperor to choose another auspicious day, and soon Yang's plot was discovered.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「無卿言，亦當致小狼狽，此亦何異滹沱之冰。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Without your words, there would still have been some disarray—how is this unlike the ice of the Hutuo River?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Even without your warning, there would still have been some disorder—but how is this unlike the ice of the Hutuo River?

sentences.zh: 轉齊國中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to become Confidential Adjunct of the Central Secretariat in the state of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Confidential Adjunct of the Central Secretariat in the state of Qi.

sentences.zh: 建元初，帶東燕令，封新陽縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he concurrently served as Magistrate of Dongyan and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinyang county.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyuan he served concurrently as magistrate of Dongyan and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinyang county.

sentences.zh: 轉羽林監，遷尚書主客郎，太尉中兵參軍，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: He became Director of the Feathered Forest Guard, was promoted to Gentleman in the Ministry of Ceremonies responsible for foreign guests, Staff Officer of the Central Army under the Grand Commandant, and concurrently Confidential Adjunct of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of the Feathered Forest Guard, was promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Ceremonies in charge of foreign guests, Staff Officer of the Central Army under the Grand Commandant, and concurrently Confidential Adjunct of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高帝疾甚，令僧真典遺詔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao's illness grew severe, he had Sengzhen supervise the drafting of his final testament.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao's illness grew grave, he had Sengzhen oversee the drafting of his final testament.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，丁父喪。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming he observed mourning for his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming he went into mourning for his father's death.

sentences.zh: 起為建威將軍，尋除南泰山太守，又為舍人。

translations.literal: Recalled to service as General Who Establishes Might, he was soon made Administrator of South Taishan, then again served as Confidential Adjunct.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning as General Who Establishes Might, he was soon appointed administrator of South Taishan and then again served as Confidential Adjunct.

sentences.zh: 僧真容貌言吐，雅有士風，武帝嘗目送之，笑曰：「人生何必計門戶，紀僧真堂堂，貴人所不及也。」

translations.literal: Sengzhen's bearing and speech had an elegant scholar's style. Emperor Wu once watched him depart and laughed, "In life why must one count one's lineage? Ji Sengzhen is truly imposing—noblemen cannot match him.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen's appearance and speech had an elegant scholar's bearing. Emperor Wu once watched him go and laughed, "In life why must one count one's lineage? Ji Sengzhen is truly imposing—noblemen cannot match him.

sentences.zh: 諸權要中最被眄遇。

translations.literal: Among all the powerful favorites he was most favored with attention.
translations.idiomatic: Among all the powerful favorites, he was the most favored.

sentences.zh: 後除前軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，開塚得五色兩頭蛇。

translations.literal: When his mother died, upon opening the tomb a five-colored two-headed serpent was found.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, a five-colored two-headed serpent was found upon opening the tomb.

sentences.zh: 武帝崩，僧真號泣思慕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu died, Sengzhen wailed and mourned in deep longing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu died, Sengzhen wailed and mourned him with deep devotion.

sentences.zh: 宋時道人楊法持與高帝有舊，元徽末，宣傳密謀。

translations.literal: During Song, the Daoist monk Yang Fachi had old ties with Emperor Gao; at the end of Yuanhui he spread word of secret plots.
translations.idiomatic: During the Song, the Daoist monk Yang Fachi had old ties with Emperor Gao. At the end of the Yuanhui era he spread word of secret plots.

sentences.zh: 升明中，以為僧正。

translations.literal: During Shengming he was made Supervisor of Monks.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengming era he was made Supervisor of Monks.

sentences.zh: 建元初，罷道，為甯朔將軍，封州陵男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he left the monastic life, became General Who Pacifies the North, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhouling.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyuan he left the monastic life, became General Who Pacifies the North, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhouling.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣法持為軍主，領支軍救援朐山。

translations.literal: In the second year Yang Fachi was dispatched as army commander to lead a subsidiary force to relieve Qushan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Yang Fachi was dispatched as army commander to lead a subsidiary force to relieve Qushan.

sentences.zh: 永明四年，坐役使將客，奪其鮭稟，削封，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming, for employing conscript soldiers as servants and seizing their salmon rations, his enfeoffment was stripped; he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongming, for using conscript soldiers as personal servants and seizing their salmon rations, his title was stripped; he died.

sentences.zh: 劉系宗

translations.literal: Liu Xizong
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xizong

sentences.zh: 劉系宗，丹陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xizong was a native of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xizong was a native of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 少便書畫，為宋竟陵王誕子景粹侍書。

translations.literal: Skilled in calligraphy and painting from youth, he served as copyist for Jingcui, son of Prince Jingling of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at calligraphy and painting from youth, he served as copyist for Jingcui, son of Prince Jingling of Song.

sentences.zh: 誕舉兵，廣陵城內皆死，敕沈慶之赦系宗，以為東宮侍書。

translations.literal: When Dan rebelled, all within Guangling city were killed; an edict from Shen Qingzhi pardoned Xizong and made him copyist in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan rebelled, everyone within Guangling city was put to death. An edict from Shen Qingzhi pardoned Xizong and made him copyist in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，為主書，以寒官累至勳品。

translations.literal: During Taishi he served as chief secretary, rising from humble posts to noble rank through merit grades.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era he served as chief secretary, rising from humble office through merit grades to noble rank.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，為奉朝請，兼中書通事舍人、員外郎，封始興南亭侯，帶秣陵令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui he was made Court Gentleman, concurrently Confidential Messenger of the Central Secretariat and Supernumerary Gentleman, enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanting in Shixing, and concurrent Magistrate of Moling.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhui he was made Court Gentleman, concurrently Confidential Messenger of the Central Secretariat and Supernumerary Gentleman, enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanting in Shixing, and concurrent magistrate of Moling.

sentences.zh: 四年，白賊唐宇之起，宿衛兵東討，遣系宗隨軍慰勞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the White Bandit Tang Yuzhi rose, the palace guard marched east to suppress him; Xizong was sent with the army to offer comfort and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when the White Bandit Tang Yuzhi rose in rebellion, the palace guard marched east to suppress him, and Xizong was sent with the army to offer comfort and rewards.

sentences.zh: 遍至遭賊郡縣，百姓被驅逼者，悉無所問，還復人伍。

translations.literal: He went everywhere to the commanderies and counties that had suffered from the rebels; common people who had been forced into service were not questioned at all and were restored to their household registers.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to every commandery and county that had suffered from the rebels. Common people who had been forced into service were not questioned at all and were restored to their household registers.

sentences.zh: 系宗還，上曰：「此段有征無戰，以時平蕩，百姓安怗，甚快也。」

translations.literal: When Xizong returned, the emperor said, "This campaign saw mobilization but no fighting; rebellion was pacified in timely fashion and the people are settled and content—very satisfying.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong returned, the emperor said, "This campaign saw mobilization but no battle. The rebellion was pacified in good time, and the people are settled and content—very satisfying.

sentences.zh: 賜系宗錢帛。

translations.literal: Xizong was granted money and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong was granted money and silk.

sentences.zh: 上欲修白下城，難於動役。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to repair the Baixia fortifications but found it difficult to mobilize labor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to repair the Baixia fortifications but found it difficult to mobilize labor.

sentences.zh: 系宗啟謫役在東人丁隨宇之為逆者，上從之。

translations.literal: Xizong proposed assigning to corvée labor the eastern households of men who had followed Yuzhi in rebellion; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong proposed assigning to corvée labor the eastern households of men who had followed Yuzhi in rebellion, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 後車駕出講武，上履行白下城曰：「劉系宗為國家得此一城。」

translations.literal: Later when the imperial carriage went out for military review, the emperor walked along the Baixia walls and said, "For the state Liu Xizong secured this entire fortification.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the imperial carriage went out for military review, the emperor walked along the Baixia walls and said, "For the state Liu Xizong secured this whole fortification.

sentences.zh: 永明中，魏使書常令系宗題答，秘書局皆隸之。

translations.literal: During Yongming, when Wei envoys sent letters, Xizong was regularly set to inscribe the replies; the Secretariat office all defer to him.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming, when Wei envoys sent letters, Xizong was regularly assigned to inscribe the replies, and the Secretariat office all deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 再為少府。

translations.literal: He twice served as Minister of the Privy Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He twice served as Minister of the Privy Treasury.

sentences.zh: 郁林即位，除甯朔將軍、宣城太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yulin acceded, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin acceded, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 系宗久在朝省，閑於職事，武帝常云：「學士輩不堪經國，唯大讀書耳。

translations.literal: Xizong had long served in court offices and was adept at administrative affairs. Emperor Wu often said, "These scholar-officials cannot manage the state—they merely read books extensively.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong had long served in court offices and was adept at administrative work. Emperor Wu often said, "These scholar-officials cannot govern the state—they merely read books at great length.

sentences.zh: 經國，一劉系宗足矣。

translations.literal: For governing the state, one Liu Xizong is enough.
translations.idiomatic: For governing the state, one Liu Xizong is enough.

sentences.zh: 沈約、王融數百人，于事何用。」

translations.literal: Of what use are Shen Yue, Wang Rong, and their hundreds for practical matters?
translations.idiomatic: Of what use are Shen Yue, Wang Rong, and their hundreds for practical affairs?

sentences.zh: 其重吏事如此。

translations.literal: Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office.

sentences.zh: 茹法亮

translations.literal: Ru Faliang
translations.idiomatic: Ru Faliang

sentences.zh: 茹法亮，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Ru Faliang was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Faliang was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 宋大明中，出身為小史。

translations.literal: During Emperor Ming of Song's Daming era he began his career as a petty clerk.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daming era of Emperor Ming of Song he began his career as a petty clerk.

sentences.zh: 曆齋幹扶侍。

translations.literal: He served successively as orderly in the fast hall and as attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as orderly in the fast hall and as attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝武末年，鞭罰過度，校獵江右，選白衣左右百八十人，皆面首富室，從至南州，得鞭者過半。

translations.literal: Near the end of Emperor Xiaowu of Song's reign, floggings were excessive. During a hunting expedition on the right bank of the Yangtze, one hundred eighty attendants in plain dress were selected—all were wealthy men of prominent households. They accompanied him to the southern regions, and more than half received floggings.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Xiaowu of Song's reign, floggings were excessive. During a hunting expedition on the right bank of the Yangtze, one hundred eighty attendants in plain dress were selected—all wealthy men from prominent households. They accompanied him to the southern regions, and more than half were flogged.

sentences.zh: 法亮憂懼，因緣啟出家得為道人。

translations.literal: Faliang, anxious and afraid, seized an opportunity to petition to leave home and become a Daoist monk.
translations.idiomatic: Anxious and afraid, Faliang seized an opportunity to petition to leave home and become a Daoist monk.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，罷道，結事阮佃夫，累至齊高帝冠軍府行參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he left the monastic life, attached himself to Ruan Dianfu, and rose to Acting Staff Officer in Emperor Gao of Qi's Champion General headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he left the monastic life, attached himself to Ruan Dianfu, and rose to Acting Staff Officer in Emperor Gao of Qi's Champion General headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及武帝鎮盆城，須舊驅使人，法亮求留為武帝江州典簽，除南台御史，帶松滋令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was garrisoned at Pencheng and needed his old runners and attendants, Faliang asked to remain as Chief Clerk of Jiangzhou for the future emperor; he was appointed Censor of the Southern Office and concurrent Magistrate of Songzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu was garrisoned at Pencheng and needed his old runners and attendants, Faliang asked to remain as Chief Clerk of Jiangzhou for the future emperor. He was appointed Censor of the Southern Office and concurrent magistrate of Songzi.

sentences.zh: 法亮便僻解事，善於承奉，稍見委信。

translations.literal: Faliang was quick-witted and capable, skilled at flattery and service, and gradually won trust.
translations.idiomatic: Faliang was quick-witted and capable, skilled at flattery and service, and gradually won trust.

sentences.zh: 建元初，度東宮主書，除奉朝請，補東宮通事舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he crossed over to serve as chief secretary in the Eastern Palace, was made Court Gentleman, and appointed Confidential Messenger in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyuan he transferred to serve as chief secretary in the Eastern Palace, was made Court Gentleman, and appointed Confidential Messenger in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，仍為中書通事舍人，除員外郎，帶南濟陰太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he remained Confidential Messenger of the Central Secretariat, was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman, and served concurrently as Administrator of South Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he remained Confidential Messenger of the Central Secretariat, was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman, and served concurrently as administrator of South Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 與會稽呂文度、臨海呂文顯並以奸佞諂事武帝。

translations.literal: Together with Lü Wendu of Kuaiji and Lü Wenxian of Linhai, he relied on sycophancy and deceit to serve Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Lü Wendu of Kuaiji and Lü Wenxian of Linhai, he relied on sycophancy and deceit to serve Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 文度為外監，專制兵權，領軍將軍守虛位而已。

translations.literal: Wendu served as Outer Supervisor with monopolistic control of military authority; the General of the Guards held nothing but an empty title.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu served as Outer Supervisor with monopolistic control of military authority, while the General of the Guards held nothing but an empty title.

sentences.zh: 天文寺常以上將星占文度吉凶。

translations.literal: The Astronomical Bureau regularly used the general's star to read Wendu's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Astronomical Bureau regularly used the general's star to read Wendu's fortune.

sentences.zh: 文度尤見委信，上嘗云：「公卿中有憂國如文度者，復何憂天下不寧。」

translations.literal: Wendu was especially trusted. The emperor once said, "If among the ministers and nobles there were one who cared for the state as Wendu does, what worry would there be that the realm would not be at peace?"
translations.idiomatic: Wendu was especially trusted. The emperor once said, "If among the ministers and nobles there were one who cared for the state as Wendu does, what worry would there be that the realm would not be at peace?"

sentences.zh: 文度既見委用，大納財賄，廣開宅宇，盛起土山，奇禽怪樹，皆聚其中，後房羅綺，王侯不能及。

translations.literal: Once Wendu was entrusted with power, he accepted bribes on a grand scale, built extensive residences, raised great artificial hills, and gathered rare birds and exotic trees within them; his rear chambers were hung with brocades that even princes and marquises could not match.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wendu was entrusted with power, he accepted bribes on a grand scale, built extensive residences, and raised great artificial hills, gathering rare birds and exotic trees within them. His rear chambers were hung with brocades that even princes and marquises could not match.

sentences.zh: 又啟上籍被卻者悉充遠戍，百姓嗟怨，或逃亡避咎。

translations.literal: He also petitioned that all whose household registers had been rejected be assigned to distant garrison duty; the people groaned in resentment, and some fled to escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned that all whose household registers had been rejected be assigned to distant garrison duty. The people groaned in resentment, and some fled to escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 富陽人唐宇之因此聚黨為亂，鼓行而東，乃于錢唐縣僭號，以新城戍為偽宮，以錢唐縣為偽太子宮，置百官皆備。

translations.literal: Tang Yuzhi of Fuyang therefore gathered followers and rebelled, marching east beating drums; at Qiantang county he usurped an imperial title, made Xincheng garrison his false palace and Qiantang county his false crown prince's palace, and installed a full set of false officials.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yuzhi of Fuyang therefore gathered followers and rebelled, marching east beating drums. At Qiantang county he usurped an imperial title, made Xincheng garrison his false palace and Qiantang county his false crown prince's palace, and installed a full set of false officials.

sentences.zh: 三吳卻籍者奔之，眾至三萬。

translations.literal: Rejected registrants from the Three Wu regions rallied to him; his force reached thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Rejected registrants from the Three Wu regions rallied to him, and his force reached thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 竊稱吳國，偽年號興平。

translations.literal: He falsely styled his realm Wu and adopted the era name Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely styled his realm Wu and adopted the era name Xingping.

sentences.zh: 其源始于虞玩之，而成于文度，事見虞玩之傳。

translations.literal: Its origins began with Yu Wanzhi and were brought to completion by Wendu; the matter is recorded in Yu Wanzhi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Its origins lay with Yu Wanzhi and were brought to completion by Wendu; the full account appears in Yu Wanzhi's biography.

sentences.zh: 法亮、文度並勢傾天下，太尉王儉常謂人曰：「我雖有大位，權寄豈及茹公。」

translations.literal: Faliang and Wendu both wielded power that dominated the realm. Grand Commandant Wang Jian often told people, "Though I hold high office, how could the delegation of authority compare with Lord Ru?
translations.idiomatic: Faliang and Wendu both wielded power that eclipsed all others. Grand Commandant Wang Jian often remarked, "Though I hold high office, how could delegated authority compare with Lord Ru?

sentences.zh: 永明二年，封望蔡縣男。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wangcai county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongming he was enfeoffed as baron of Wangcai county.

sentences.zh: 七年，除臨淮太守，轉竟陵王司徒中兵參軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Administrator of Linhuai and transferred to Staff Officer of Central Troops under the Chamberlain's headquarters for Prince Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed administrator of Linhuai and transferred to staff officer of central troops under Prince Jingling's chamberlain headquarters.

sentences.zh: 巴東王子響于荊州殺僚佐，上遣軍西上，使法亮宣旨安撫子響。

translations.literal: Prince Zixiang of Badong killed his staff officers in Jingzhou; the emperor dispatched troops westward and sent Faliang to proclaim the imperial will and pacify Zixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zixiang of Badong killed his staff officers in Jingzhou. The emperor dispatched troops westward and sent Faliang to proclaim the imperial will and pacify him.

sentences.zh: 法亮至江津，子響呼法亮，疑畏不肯往。

translations.literal: When Faliang reached Jiangjin, Zixiang summoned him, but Faliang, suspicious and afraid, refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Faliang reached Jiangjin, Zixiang summoned him, but Faliang, suspicious and afraid, refused to go.

sentences.zh: 又求見傳詔，法亮又不遣。

translations.literal: Zixiang also requested to see the edict-bearer, and Faliang again would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang also asked to see the edict-bearer, and Faliang again refused to send him.

sentences.zh: 故子響怒，遣兵破尹略軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zixiang grew angry and sent troops to crush Yin Lue's army.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang thereupon grew angry and sent troops to crush Yin Lue's army.

sentences.zh: 事平，法亮至江陵，誅賞處分，皆稱敕斷決。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Faliang went to Jiangling; executions, rewards, and dispositions all were said to have been decided by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Once the affair was settled, Faliang went to Jiangling. Executions, rewards, and dispositions were all said to have been decided by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 軍還，上悔誅子響，法亮被責，少時親任如舊。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the emperor regretted executing Zixiang; Faliang was rebuked, but before long he was trusted as intimately as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, the emperor regretted executing Zixiang. Faliang was rebuked, but before long he enjoyed the emperor's intimate trust as before.

sentences.zh: 廣開宅宇，杉齋光麗，與延昌殿相埒。

translations.literal: He greatly expanded his residence; his cedar hall was bright and splendid, matching the Yanchang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly expanded his residence. His cedar hall was bright and splendid, rivaling the Yanchang Hall.

sentences.zh: 延昌殿，武帝中齋也。

translations.literal: Yanchang Hall was Emperor Wu's inner fast hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchang Hall was Emperor Wu's inner fast hall.

sentences.zh: 宅後為魚池釣台，土山樓館，長廊將一里。

translations.literal: Behind the residence were a fish pond and angling terrace, earthen hills with pavilions, and a corridor nearly a li long.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the residence lay a fish pond and angling terrace, earthen hills with pavilions, and a corridor nearly a li in length.

sentences.zh: 竹林花藥之美，公家苑囿所不能及。

translations.literal: The beauty of its bamboo groves, flowers, and herbs surpassed what the palace gardens could match.
translations.idiomatic: The beauty of its bamboo groves, flowers, and medicinal plants surpassed even the imperial gardens.

sentences.zh: 郁林即位，除步兵校尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yulin ascended the throne, Faliang was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin ascended the throne, Faliang was appointed commandant of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 時有綦母珍之，居舍人之任，凡所論薦，事無不允。

translations.literal: At this time there was Qimu Zhenzhi, who held the post of attendant; whatever nominations he put forward were invariably approved.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Qimu Zhenzhi held the post of attendant, and whatever nominations he put forward were invariably approved.

sentences.zh: 內外要職及郡丞尉，皆論價而後施行。

translations.literal: Important posts inside and outside the court, as well as county assistant magistrates and commandants, all were sold by negotiated price before appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Important posts inside and outside the court, as well as county assistant magistrates and commandants, were all sold by negotiated price before appointment.

sentences.zh: 貨賄交至，旬月之間，累至千金。

translations.literal: Bribes flowed in without cease; within a month or so they accumulated to a thousand gold pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Bribes poured in without cease, and within a month or so they accumulated to a thousand gold pieces.

sentences.zh: 帝給珍之宅，宅邊又有空宅，從即並取，輒令材官營作，不關詔旨。

translations.literal: The emperor granted Zhenzhi a residence; there was another empty residence beside it, which he took on the spot as well, then ordered the construction officer to build there without reference to an edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted Zhenzhi a residence. There was another empty residence beside it, which he seized on the spot as well, then ordered the construction officer to build there without any imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 材官將軍細作丞相語云：「寧拒至尊敕，不可違舍人命。」

translations.literal: The construction officer general finely mimicked the prime minister's speech, saying, "Better to refuse the supreme sovereign's edict than to disobey an attendant's order.
translations.idiomatic: The construction officer general wittily echoed the prime minister's words: "Better to refuse the supreme sovereign's edict than to disobey an attendant's order.

sentences.zh: 珍之母隨弟欽之作暨陽令，欽之罷縣還，珍之迎母至湖熟，輒將青氅百人自隨，鼓角橫吹，都下富人追從者百數。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi's mother followed his younger brother Qinzhi when the latter served as magistrate of Jiyang; when Qinzhi left office and returned, Zhenzhi went to meet his mother at Hushu, bringing with him a hundred green-cloaked guards, with drums, horns, and wind instruments playing; wealthy men of the capital followed in scores.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi's mother had accompanied his younger brother Qinzhi when the latter served as magistrate of Jiyang. When Qinzhi left office and returned, Zhenzhi went to meet his mother at Hushu with a hundred green-cloaked guards, drums, horns, and wind instruments playing, and scores of wealthy men of the capital followed in his train.

sentences.zh: 欽之自行佐作縣，還除廬陵王驃騎正將軍，又詐宣敕使欽之領青氅。

translations.literal: Qinzhi had himself served as assistant magistrate in the county; on his return he was appointed Regular General under the Fast Cavalry headquarters of the Prince of Luling, and Zhenzhi also falsely proclaimed an edict appointing Qinzhi to command the green-cloaked guards.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhi had himself served as assistant magistrate in the county. On his return he was appointed regular general under the Prince of Luling's fast cavalry headquarters, and Zhenzhi also falsely proclaimed an edict appointing Qinzhi to command the green-cloaked guards.

sentences.zh: 珍之有一銅鏡，背有「三公」字，常語人云：「征祥如此，何患三公不至。」

translations.literal: Zhenzhi had a bronze mirror with the characters "Three Dukes" on the back; he often told people, "With such an omen, why worry that the rank of Three Dukes will not come?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi owned a bronze mirror with the characters "Three Dukes" on the back. He often told people, "With such an omen, why worry that the rank of Three Dukes will not come?"

sentences.zh: 乃就蔣王廟乞願得三公，封郡王。

translations.literal: He went to the Temple of Prince Jiang to pray for attainment of the Three Dukes and enfeoffment as a commandery prince.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the Temple of Prince Jiang to pray that he might attain the Three Dukes and be enfeoffed as a commandery prince.

sentences.zh: 啟帝求封，朝議未許。

translations.literal: He petitioned the emperor for enfeoffment, but court deliberation did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned the emperor for enfeoffment, but the court deliberation did not approve.

sentences.zh: 又自陳曰：「珍之西州伏事，侍從入宮，契闊心膂，竭盡誠力。

translations.literal: He also declared in his own person, "Zhenzhi served humbly in the Western Province, followed into the palace, shared hardships heart and soul, and exhausted my loyalty and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He also declared in person, "Zhenzhi served humbly in the Western Province, followed the emperor into the palace, shared hardships heart and soul, and exhausted my loyalty and strength.

sentences.zh: 王融奸謀潛構，自非珍之翼衛扶持，事在不測。

translations.literal: Wang Rong secretly plotted treachery; had it not been for Zhenzhi's protection and support, the outcome would have been unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong secretly plotted treachery. Had it not been for Zhenzhi's protection and support, the outcome would have been unpredictable.

sentences.zh: 今惜千戶侯，誰為官使者。」

translations.literal: Now if you begrudge me a marquisate of a thousand households, who will serve as your agent at court?
translations.idiomatic: If you begrudge me now a marquisate of a thousand households, who will serve as your agent at court?

sentences.zh: 又有牒自論於朝廷曰：「當世祖晏駕之時，內外紛擾，珍之手抱至尊，口行處分，忠誠契闊，人誰不知。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial arguing before the court, "At the time of Emperor Shizu's death, turmoil reigned within and without; Zhenzhi held the supreme sovereign in his arms and issued orders by word of mouth—such loyal devotion in hardship is known to all.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial arguing before the court, "When Emperor Shizu passed away, turmoil reigned within and without. Zhenzhi held the sovereign in his arms and issued orders by word of mouth—such loyal devotion in hardship is known to all.

sentences.zh: 今希千戶侯，於分非過。」

translations.literal: To hope now for a marquisate of a thousand households would not exceed my due."
translations.idiomatic: To hope now for a marquisate of a thousand households would not exceed my due."

sentences.zh: 乃許三百戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was granted three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 瞋恚形於言色，進為五百戶，又不肯受。

translations.literal: Anger showed in his speech and countenance; the grant was raised to five hundred households, yet he still refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Anger showed in his speech and countenance. The grant was raised to five hundred households, yet he still refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 明帝議誅之，乃許封汝南縣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming deliberated on executing him, he finally granted enfeoffment as Count of Runan county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming deliberated on executing him, the court finally granted him enfeoffment as count of Runan county.

sentences.zh: 有杜文謙者，吳郡錢唐人。

translations.literal: There was one Du Wenqian, a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Du Wenqian, a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝為南郡王，文謙侍五經文句，曆太學博士。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Nanjun, Wenqian attended him in the commentary on the Five Classics and served successively as Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was Prince of Nanjun, Wenqian attended him in the commentary on the Five Classics and served in turn as erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 出為溧陽令，未之職。

translations.literal: He was sent out as magistrate of Liyang but never took up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as magistrate of Liyang but never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 會明帝知權，蕭諶用事，文謙乃謂珍之曰：「天下事可知，灰盡粉滅，匪朝伊夕，不早為計，吾徒無類矣。」

translations.literal: Just as Emperor Ming seized power and Xiao Chen held sway, Wenqian said to Zhenzhi, "The course of affairs under heaven is clear: we shall be reduced to ashes and dust, and not over many days. If we do not plan early, our kind will be wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Emperor Ming seized power and Xiao Chen held sway, Wenqian said to Zhenzhi, "The course of affairs is clear: we shall be reduced to ashes and dust, and not over many days. If we do not plan early, our kind will be wiped out.

sentences.zh: 珍之曰：「計將安出？」

translations.literal: Zhenzhi said, "What plan do you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi said, "What plan do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「先帝故人多見擯斥，今召而使之，誰不慷慨。

translations.literal: He replied, "Many of the late emperor's old associates have been cast aside; summon them now and put them to use—who would not respond with ardor?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Many of the late emperor's old associates have been cast aside. Summon them now and put them to use—who would not respond with ardor?

sentences.zh: 近聞王洪范與趙越常、徐僧亮、萬靈會共語，皆攘袂捶床。

translations.literal: Recently I heard Wang Hongfan discussing matters with Zhao Yuechang, Xu Sengliang, and Wan Linghui; all rolled up their sleeves and pounded the bed.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I heard Wang Hongfan discussing matters with Zhao Yuechang, Xu Sengliang, and Wan Linghui. All of them rolled up their sleeves and pounded the bed.

sentences.zh: 君其密報周奉叔，使萬靈會、魏僧勉殺蕭諶，則宮內之兵皆我用也。

translations.literal: Secretly inform Zhou Fengshu and have Wan Linghui and Wei Sengmian kill Xiao Chen—then all the troops within the palace will be ours.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly inform Zhou Fengshu and have Wan Linghui and Wei Sengmian kill Xiao Chen—then all the troops within the palace will be ours.

sentences.zh: 即勒兵入尚書斬蕭令，兩都伯力耳。

translations.literal: Then march the troops into the Secretariat and execute Director Xiao—a matter of two wardens' strength.
translations.idiomatic: Then march the troops into the Secretariat and execute Director Xiao—a matter requiring no more than two wardens' strength.

sentences.zh: 其次則遣荊軻、豫讓之徒，因諮事，左手頓其胸，則方寸之刃，足以立事，亦萬世一時也。

translations.literal: Failing that, send men like Jing Ke and Yu Rang: under pretense of consultation, press against the chest with the left hand, and a blade an inch in size will suffice to accomplish the deed—it would be an opportunity of ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Failing that, send men like Jing Ke and Yu Rang. Under pretense of consultation, press against the chest with the left hand, and a blade an inch long will suffice to accomplish the deed—an opportunity that comes once in ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 今舉大事亦死，不舉事亦死，二死等耳，死社稷可乎。

translations.literal: To raise a great affair now is death; not to raise it is also death—the two deaths are equal. Is it not better to die for the altars of state?
translations.idiomatic: To raise a great affair now means death; not to raise it also means death—the two deaths are equal. Is it not better to die for the altars of state?

sentences.zh: 若遲疑不斷，復少日，錄君稱敕賜死，父母為殉，在眼中矣。」

translations.literal: If you hesitate and do not decide, in a few more days the Lord Recorder will proclaim an edict ordering your death, and your parents will die as well—the prospect is before our eyes."
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate and do not decide, in a few more days the Lord Recorder will proclaim an edict ordering your death, and your parents will die as well—the prospect is before our eyes."

sentences.zh: 珍之不能用。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi would not adopt his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi would not adopt his plan.

sentences.zh: 時徐龍駒亦當得封，珍之恥與龍駒共詔，因求別立。

translations.literal: At this time Xu Longju was also due to receive enfeoffment; Zhenzhi was ashamed to share an edict with Longju and therefore asked for separate creation.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Xu Longju was also due to receive enfeoffment. Zhenzhi was ashamed to share an edict with Longju and therefore asked for a separate patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 事未及行而事敗。

translations.literal: Before the matter could be carried out, the plot failed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the matter could be carried out, the plot failed.

sentences.zh: 珍之在西州時有一手板，相者云：「當貴」。

translations.literal: When Zhenzhi was in the Western Province he had a hand tablet; a physiognomist said, "You will attain noble rank."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzhi was in the Western Province he had a hand tablet. A physiognomist said, "You will attain noble rank."

sentences.zh: 每以此言動帝，又圖黃門郎，帝嘗問之曰：「西州時手板何在？」

translations.literal: He often used this remark to move the emperor, and also coveted the post of Gentleman of the Yellow Gates; the emperor once asked him, "Where is the hand tablet from the Western Province?
translations.idiomatic: He often used this remark to move the emperor and also coveted the post of gentleman of the Yellow Gates. The emperor once asked him, "Where is the hand tablet from the Western Province?

sentences.zh: 珍之曰：「此是黃門手板，官何須問？」

translations.literal: Zhenzhi said, "This is a Yellow Gates hand tablet—why does Your Majesty need to ask?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi said, "This is a Yellow Gates hand tablet—why does Your Majesty need to ask?"

sentences.zh: 帝大笑。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed heartily.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed heartily.

sentences.zh: 珍之時為左將軍、南彭城太守，領中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: At that time Zhenzhi was General of the Left, Administrator of South Pengcheng, and concurrent Attendant for Current Affairs in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhenzhi was general of the left, administrator of South Pengcheng, and concurrent Secretariat attendant for current affairs.

sentences.zh: 正直宿，宣旨使即往蔣王廟祈福，因收送廷尉，與周奉叔、杜文謙同死。

translations.literal: While on duty overnight, he was sent by imperial decree to the Temple of Prince Jiang to pray for blessings, and there was seized and delivered to the Minister of Justice, dying together with Zhou Fengshu and Du Wenqian.
translations.idiomatic: While on overnight duty, he was sent by imperial decree to the Temple of Prince Jiang to pray for blessings. There he was seized and delivered to the Minister of Justice, and died together with Zhou Fengshu and Du Wenqian.

sentences.zh: 文謙有學行，善言吐。

translations.literal: Wenqian had learning and conduct and excelled in speech.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqian had learning and integrity and excelled in speech.

sentences.zh: 其父聞其死，曰：「吾所以憂者，恐其不得死地耳。

translations.literal: When his father heard of his death he said, "What I feared was that he might not die a worthy death.
translations.idiomatic: When his father heard of his death he said, "What I feared was that he might not die a worthy death.

sentences.zh: 今以忠義死，復何恨哉。

translations.literal: To die now for loyalty and righteousness—what regret remains?
translations.idiomatic: To die now for loyalty and righteousness—what regret remains?

sentences.zh: 王經母所以欣經之義也。」

translations.literal: This is why Wang Jing's mother rejoiced in Wang Jing's righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Wang Jing's mother rejoiced in Wang Jing's righteousness.

sentences.zh: 時人美其言。

translations.literal: People of the time praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time praised his words.

sentences.zh: 龍駒以奄人本給安陸侯，後度東宮為齋帥。

translations.literal: Longju, as a eunuch, had originally served the Marquis of Anlu; later he passed through the Eastern Palace to become master of the fast hall.
translations.idiomatic: Longju, a eunuch, had originally served the Marquis of Anlu. Later he passed through the Eastern Palace to become master of the fast hall.

sentences.zh: 帝即位後，以便佞見寵。

translations.literal: After the emperor ascended the throne, he won favor through flattery and servility.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor ascended the throne, he won favor through flattery and servility.

sentences.zh: 凡諸鄙黷雜事，皆所誘勸。

translations.literal: All sorts of vulgar and profane diversions were instigated and encouraged by him.
translations.idiomatic: All sorts of vulgar and profane diversions were instigated and encouraged by him.

sentences.zh: 位羽林監、後合舍人、黃門署令、淮陵太守。

translations.literal: His posts included Inspector of the Feathered Forest Guard, Attendant of the Rear Chamber, Director of the Yellow Gates Office, and Administrator of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: His posts included inspector of the Feathered Forest Guard, attendant of the rear chamber, director of the Yellow Gates Office, and administrator of Huailing.

sentences.zh: 帝為龍駒置嬪御妓樂。

translations.literal: The emperor provided Longju with concubines and musicians.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor provided Longju with concubines and musicians.

sentences.zh: 常住含章殿，著黃綸帽，被貂裘，南面向案，代帝畫敕。

translations.literal: He usually resided in Hanchang Hall, wore a yellow silk cap and sable fur, faced south before a desk, and drafted edicts in the emperor's place.
translations.idiomatic: He usually resided in Hanchang Hall, wore a yellow silk cap and sable fur, faced south before a desk, and drafted edicts in the emperor's place.

sentences.zh: 內左右侍直，與帝不異。

translations.literal: Attendants at left and right inside were no different from those of the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants at left and right within were no different from those of the emperor.

sentences.zh: 前代趙忠、張讓之徒，莫之能比。

translations.literal: Not even men like Zhao Zhong and Zhang Rang of former times could compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: Not even men like Zhao Zhong and Zhang Rang of former times could compare with him.

sentences.zh: 封惠懷縣男，事未行，明帝請誅之，懇至，乃見許。

translations.literal: He was to be enfeoffed as Baron of Huihuai county, but before the matter was carried out, Emperor Ming pleaded earnestly for his execution and was finally granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: He was to be enfeoffed as baron of Huihuai county, but before the matter was carried out Emperor Ming pleaded earnestly for his execution and was finally granted permission.

sentences.zh: 曹道剛，廢帝之日直合省，蕭諶先入，若欲論事，兵隨後奄進，以刀刺之，洞胸死，因進宮內廢帝。

translations.literal: Cao Daogang: on the day the emperor was deposed he was on duty in the Combined Chambers Office; Xiao Chen entered first, as if to discuss affairs, then soldiers suddenly rushed in from behind, stabbed him with a knife through the chest, and he died; they then entered the palace and deposed the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Daogang: on the day the emperor was deposed he was on duty in the Combined Chambers Office. Xiao Chen entered first, as if to discuss affairs, then soldiers suddenly rushed in from behind, stabbed him through the chest, and killed him. They then entered the palace and deposed the emperor.

sentences.zh: 直後徐僧亮甚怒，大言於眾曰：「吾等荷恩，今日應死報。」

translations.literal: Attendant Supervisor Xu Sengliang was greatly angered and declared loudly before the crowd, "We have received grace—today we should repay with our deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant supervisor Xu Sengliang was greatly angered and declared loudly before the crowd, "We have received grace—today we should repay with our deaths.

sentences.zh: 又見殺。

translations.literal: He too was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He too was killed.

sentences.zh: 道剛字景昭，彭城人，性質直。

translations.literal: Daogang, courtesy name Jingzhao, was a native of Pengcheng and upright in nature.
translations.idiomatic: Daogang, courtesy name Jingzhao, was a native of Pengcheng and upright by nature.

sentences.zh: 帝雖與之狎而未嘗敢詶。

translations.literal: Though the emperor was intimate with him, he never dared to answer back.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor was intimate with him, he never dared to answer back.

sentences.zh: 帝悅市里雜事，以為歡樂。

translations.literal: The emperor delighted in vulgar street amusements as his entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor delighted in vulgar street amusements as his entertainment.

sentences.zh: 道剛輒避之。

translations.literal: Daogang always kept away from such things.
translations.idiomatic: Daogang always kept away from such things.

sentences.zh: 益州人韓護善騎馬，帝嘗呼入華林園令騎，大賞狎之。

translations.literal: Han Hu of Yizhou was skilled at horsemanship; the emperor once summoned him into the Hualin Garden to ride and greatly rewarded and indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hu of Yizhou was skilled at horsemanship. The emperor once summoned him into the Hualin Garden to ride and greatly rewarded and indulged him.

sentences.zh: 道剛出謂明帝：「主上猶是小兒，左右皆須正人，使日見禮則。

translations.literal: Daogang went out and said to Emperor Ming, "Our sovereign is still a young boy—the attendants around him must all be upright men, so that he may daily witness ritual and propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Daogang went out and said to Emperor Ming, "Our sovereign is still a young boy—the attendants around him must all be upright men, so that he may daily witness ritual and propriety.

sentences.zh: 近聞韓護與天子齊馬並馳，此導人君于危地，道剛欲殺之。」

translations.literal: Recently I heard Han Hu and the Son of Heaven racing horses side by side—this leads the ruler onto dangerous ground; I, Daogang, intend to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I heard Han Hu and the Son of Heaven racing horses side by side—this leads the ruler onto dangerous ground. I, Daogang, intend to kill him.

sentences.zh: 既而遣人刺殺護。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he sent men to assassinate Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he sent men to assassinate Hu.

sentences.zh: 及道剛死，張融謂劉繪曰：「道剛似不為諂，亦復不免也。」

translations.literal: When Daogang died, Zhang Rong said to Liu Hui, "Daogang seems not to have been flattering, yet he still could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: When Daogang died, Zhang Rong said to Liu Hui, "Daogang seems not to have been a flatterer, yet he still could not escape.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「夫徑寸之珠，非不寶也，而蚌之所病，云何不療之哉，此道剛所以死也。」

translations.literal: Liu replied, "A pearl an inch across is indeed a treasure, yet it is what afflicts the clam—how could one not treat the affliction? That is why Daogang died."
translations.idiomatic: Liu answered, "A pearl an inch across is no less a treasure, yet it is what sickens the clam—how could one not cure the sickness? That is why Daogang had to die."

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，高、武舊人鮮有存者，法亮以主署文事，故不見疑，位任如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, few of the old associates of Gao and Wu survived; Faliang, because he chiefly handled documentary affairs, was not suspected and retained his post and duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, few of the old associates of Gao and Wu survived. Faliang, because he chiefly handled documentary affairs, was not suspected and retained his post and duties as before.

sentences.zh: 先是延昌殿為武帝陰室，藏諸服御，二少帝並居西殿。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yanchang Hall had served as Emperor Wu's private chamber, storing his robes and accoutrements; the two young emperors both resided in the West Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yanchang Hall had served as Emperor Wu's private chamber, storing his robes and accoutrements. The two young emperors both resided in the West Hall.

sentences.zh: 及明帝居東齋，開陰室，出武帝白紗帽、防身刀，法亮歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took up residence in the Eastern Fast Hall and opened the private chamber, bringing out Emperor Wu's white gauze cap and personal dagger, Faliang sobbed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took up residence in the Eastern Fast Hall and opened the private chamber, bringing out Emperor Wu's white gauze cap and personal dagger, Faliang sobbed and wept.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，王敬則事平，法亮復受敕宣慰諸郡，無所納受。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, after Wang Jingze's revolt was settled, Faliang again received orders to proclaim comfort to the various commanderies and accepted no gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai, after Wang Jingze's revolt was settled, Faliang again received orders to proclaim comfort to the various commanderies and accepted no gifts.

sentences.zh: 東昏即位，出法亮為大司農。

translations.literal: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, Faliang was transferred out as Minister of Grand Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, Faliang was transferred out as minister of grand agriculture.

sentences.zh: 中書權利之職，法亮不樂去，固辭不受。

translations.literal: The Secretariat was the post of power and profit; Faliang was unwilling to leave and firmly declined, refusing to accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was the post of power and profit. Faliang was unwilling to leave and firmly declined, refusing to accept.

sentences.zh: 既而代人已到，法亮垂涕而出，卒官。

translations.literal: Before long his replacement arrived; Faliang wept as he departed and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his replacement arrived. Faliang wept as he departed and died in office.

sentences.zh: 呂文顯

translations.literal: Lü Wenxian
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wenxian

sentences.zh: 呂文顯，臨海人也。

translations.literal: Lü Wenxian was a native of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wenxian was a native of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 升明初，為齊高帝錄尚書省事，累遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengming he served in Emperor Gao of Qi's Office for Recording Affairs of the Master of Writing and rose successively to Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shengming he served in Emperor Gao of Qi's office for recording affairs of the Master of Writing and rose in turn to palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 後為秣陵令，封劉陽縣男。

translations.literal: Later he became magistrate of Molin and was enfeoffed as Baron of Liuyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became magistrate of Molin and was enfeoffed as baron of Liuyang county.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，為中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming he became Attendant for Current Affairs in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming he became Secretariat attendant for current affairs.

sentences.zh: 文顯臨事以刻核被知。

translations.literal: Wenxian became known for handling affairs with harsh exactingness.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxian became known for handling affairs with harsh exactingness.

sentences.zh: 三年，帶南清河太守，與茹法亮等疊出入為舍人，並見親幸。

translations.literal: In the third year he concurrently served as Administrator of South Qinghe; alternating in and out with Ru Faliang and others as attendants, he was all similarly favored.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he concurrently served as administrator of South Qinghe. Alternating in and out with Ru Faliang and others as attendants, he was similarly favored.

sentences.zh: 多四方餉遺，並造大宅，聚山開池。

translations.literal: He received many gifts from all quarters and built a great mansion, piling up hills and opening ponds.
translations.idiomatic: He received many gifts from all quarters and built a great mansion, piling up hills and opening ponds.

sentences.zh: 時中書舍人四人各住一省，世謂之四戶。

translations.literal: At this time the four Secretariat attendants each held one bureau; the world called them the Four Households.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the four Secretariat attendants each held one bureau; the world called them the Four Households.

sentences.zh: 既總重權，勢傾天下。

translations.literal: Having combined great power in their hands, their influence dominated the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Having combined great power in their hands, their influence eclipsed all others.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋舊制，宰人之官，以六年為限，近世以六年過久，又以三周為期，謂之小滿。

translations.literal: Under the old system of Jin and Song, the term for posts administering the people was fixed at six years; in recent times six years was considered too long, and a cycle of three years was set, called the "small full term."
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system of Jin and Song, the term for posts administering the people was fixed at six years. In recent times six years was considered too long, and a cycle of three years was set, called the "small full term."

sentences.zh: 而遷換去來，又不依三周之制，送故迎新，吏人疲于道路。

translations.literal: Yet transfers and replacements coming and going no longer followed the three-year system; seeing off the old and welcoming the new left clerks and people exhausted on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Yet transfers and replacements coming and going no longer followed the three-year system. Seeing off the old and welcoming the new left clerks and people exhausted on the roads.

sentences.zh: 四方守宰餉遺，一年咸數百萬。

translations.literal: Governors and magistrates from all quarters sent gifts and presents; within a year each received several million.
translations.idiomatic: Officials throughout the realm showered them with gifts and presents; within a year each household took in several million.

sentences.zh: 舍人茹法亮於眾中語人曰：「何須覓外祿，此一戶內年辦百萬。」

translations.literal: Attendant Ru Faliang said to people in the crowd: "Why bother seeking outside emoluments? Within this one household we can produce a million a year.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Ru Faliang said to people in the crowd: "Why bother seeking outside emoluments? Within this one household we can produce a million a year.

sentences.zh: 蓋約言之也。

translations.literal: That was only a rough way of putting it.
translations.idiomatic: That was only a rough way of putting it.

sentences.zh: 其後玄象失度，史官奏宜修祈禳之禮。

translations.literal: After this celestial phenomena fell out of their proper courses, the historiographers memorialized that prayer and exorcism rites ought to be performed.
translations.idiomatic: After this, heaven's signs fell out of order, and the historiographers memorialized that prayer and exorcism rites ought to be performed.

sentences.zh: 王儉聞之，謂上曰：「天文乖忤，此禍由四戶。」

translations.literal: Wang Jian heard of this and said to the emperor: "Heaven's signs are at odds—this calamity arises from the Four Households.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian heard of this and said to the emperor: "Heaven's signs are at odds—this calamity arises from the Four Households.

sentences.zh: 仍奏文顯等專擅愆和，極言其事。

translations.literal: He then memorialized that Wenxian and the others had monopolized power and disrupted harmony, speaking to the full extent of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized that Wenxian and the others had monopolized power and disrupted harmony, speaking to the full extent of the matter.

sentences.zh: 上雖納之而不能改也。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this but could not change the situation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this but could not change the situation.

sentences.zh: 文顯累遷左中郎將，南東莞太守。

translations.literal: Wenxian rose in successive appointments to Left Commandant of Gentlemen and Administrator of South Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxian rose in turn to left commandant of gentlemen and administrator of South Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 故事，府州部內論事，皆簽前直敘所論之事，後雲謹簽，日月下又云某官某簽，故府州置典簽以典之。

translations.literal: By precedent, when prefectures and provinces deliberated on matters within their jurisdictions, documents first stated directly what was under discussion, then bore the words "respectfully endorsed," and beneath the date appeared "endorsed by such-and-such an official." Hence prefectures and provinces appointed chief clerks to manage this.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when prefectures and provinces deliberated on matters within their jurisdictions, documents first stated directly what was under discussion, then bore the words "respectfully endorsed," and beneath the date appeared "endorsed by such-and-such an official." Hence prefectures and provinces appointed chief clerks to manage this.

sentences.zh: 本五品吏，宋初改為七職。

translations.literal: Originally fifth-rank clerks, at the beginning of Song the post was changed to seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Originally fifth-rank clerks, at the beginning of Song the post was changed to seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 宋氏晚運，多以幼少皇子為方鎮，時主皆以親近左右領典簽，典簽之權稍重。

translations.literal: In the late years of the Song house, many young princes were placed in regional commands, and the reigning monarchs all put their close attendants in charge of the chief clerks, so the chief clerks' power grew somewhat heavier.
translations.idiomatic: In the late years of the Song house, many young princes were placed in regional commands, and the reigning monarchs all put their close attendants in charge of the chief clerks, so the chief clerks' power grew somewhat heavier.

sentences.zh: 大明、泰始，長王臨蕃，素族出鎮，莫不皆出內教命，刺史不得專其任也。

translations.literal: During Daming and Taishi, when elder princes held frontier posts and men of common lineage went out to command garrisons, nothing was done without orders from the inner court, and regional inspectors could not hold full authority in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: During Daming and Taishi, when elder princes held frontier posts and men of common lineage went out to command garrisons, nothing was done without orders from the inner court, and regional inspectors could not hold full authority in their duties.

sentences.zh: 宗愨為豫州，吳喜公為典簽。

translations.literal: When Zong Que was at Yuzhou, Wu Xigong served as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Que was at Yuzhou, Wu Xigong served as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 愨刑政所施，喜公每多違執。

translations.literal: In the punishments and policies Que imposed, Xigong often countermanded and obstructed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the punishments and policies Que imposed, Xigong often countermanded and obstructed him.

sentences.zh: 愨大怒曰：「宗愨年將六十，為國竭命，政得一州如鬥大，不能復與典簽共臨！」

translations.literal: Que raged and said: "Zong Que is nearly sixty, expending his life for the state, and ought to command a province barely the size of a dipper—I cannot share governance again with a chief clerk!
translations.idiomatic: Que raged and said: "Zong Que is nearly sixty, expending his life for the state, and ought to command a province barely the size of a dipper—I cannot share governance again with a chief clerk!

sentences.zh: 喜公稽顙流血乃止。

translations.literal: Only when Xigong knocked his forehead to the ground until it bled did Que relent.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Xigong knocked his forehead to the ground until it bled did Que relent.

sentences.zh: 自此以後，權寄彌隆，典簽遞互還都，一歲數反，時主輒與閑言，訪以方事。

translations.literal: From this time on delegated power grew ever more lofty; chief clerks rotated in returning to the capital several times in a year, and the reigning monarch would talk with them at leisure and inquire about regional affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From this time on delegated power grew ever loftier. Chief clerks rotated in returning to the capital several times a year, and the reigning monarch would talk with them at leisure and inquire about regional affairs.

sentences.zh: 刺史行事之美惡，系於典簽之口，莫不折節推奉，恒慮不及。

translations.literal: Whether a regional inspector's conduct was good or bad depended on the chief clerk's word; none failed to defer and fawn upon him, ever fearing they had not done enough.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a regional inspector's conduct was good or bad depended on the chief clerk's word; none failed to defer and fawn upon him, ever fearing they had not done enough.

sentences.zh: 於是威行州郡，權重蕃君。

translations.literal: Thus their authority prevailed through the provinces and commanderies, and their power outweighed that of the frontier lords.
translations.idiomatic: Thus their authority prevailed through the provinces and commanderies, and their power outweighed that of the frontier lords.

sentences.zh: 劉道濟、柯孟孫等奸慝髮露，雖即顯戮，而權任之重不異。

translations.literal: When the wickedness of Liu Daoji, Ke Mengsun, and others was exposed, though they were immediately executed in public, the weight of the office's power was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the wickedness of Liu Daoji, Ke Mengsun, and others was exposed, though they were immediately executed in public, the weight of the office's power was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明帝輔政，深知之，始制諸州急事宜密有所論，不得遣典簽還都，而典簽之任輕矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming served as regent, having seen this clearly, he first decreed that urgent matters in the provinces should be discussed in secret and that chief clerks must not be sent back to the capital—and so the chief clerk's post grew lighter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming served as regent, having seen this clearly, he first decreed that urgent matters in the provinces should be discussed in secret and that chief clerks must not be sent back to the capital—and so the chief clerk's post grew lighter.

sentences.zh: 後以文顯守少府，見任使，曆建武、永元之世，至尚書右丞，少府卿，卒官。

translations.literal: Later Wenxian was appointed to hold the Ministry of the Privy Purse; he continued to be employed through the Jianwu and Yongyuan eras, rising to Right Vice Director in the Master of Writing, Minister of the Privy Purse, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wenxian was appointed to hold the Ministry of the Privy Purse. He continued to be employed through the Jianwu and Yongyuan eras, rising to right vice director in the Master of Writing and minister of the privy purse, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 茹法珍

translations.literal: Ru Fazhen
translations.idiomatic: Ru Fazhen

sentences.zh: 茹法珍，會稽人，梅蟲兒，吳興人，齊東昏時並為制局監，俱見愛幸。

translations.literal: Ru Fazhen was a native of Kuaiji; Mei Chonge was a native of Wuxing. Under Emperor Donghun of Qi they both served as directors of the arsenal bureau and were alike favored and cherished.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Fazhen was a native of Kuaiji; Mei Chonge was a native of Wuxing. Under Emperor Donghun of Qi they both served as directors of the arsenal bureau and were alike favored and cherished.

sentences.zh: 自江祏、始安王遙光等誅後，及左右應敕捉刀之徒並專國命，人間謂之刀敕，權奪人主。

translations.literal: After Jiang Si, Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an, and the others were executed, those attendants and imperial edict drafters on the emperor's left and right together monopolized the nation's commands; people called them "blade-edicts," for their power usurped the sovereign's.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiang Si, Prince Yao Guang of Shi'an, and the others were executed, the attendants and imperial edict drafters at the emperor's side together monopolized the nation's commands. People called them "blade-edicts," for their power usurped the sovereign's.

sentences.zh: 都下為之語曰：「欲求貴職依刀敕，須得富豪事禦刀。」

translations.literal: The capital had a saying about it: "To seek a noble post, rely on the blade-edicts; you must be rich enough to wait upon the imperial blade."
translations.idiomatic: The capital had a saying about it: "To seek a noble post, rely on the blade-edicts; you must be rich enough to wait upon the imperial blade."

sentences.zh: 時又有新蔡人徐世檦，尤見寵信，自殿內主帥為直合驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: At this time there was also Xu Shibiao of Xincai, who was especially favored and trusted; from commander within the palace halls he was made General of Valiant Cavalry for the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At this time there was also Xu Shibiao of Xincai, who was especially favored and trusted; from commander within the palace halls he was made general of valiant cavalry for the Direct Gate.

sentences.zh: 凡諸殺戮，皆世檦所勸。

translations.literal: Every execution was urged by Shibiao.
translations.idiomatic: Every execution was urged by Shibiao.

sentences.zh: 殺徐孝嗣後，封臨汝縣子。

translations.literal: After Xu Xiaosi was killed, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Linru county.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Xiaosi was killed, he was enfeoffed as viscount of Linru county.

sentences.zh: 陳顯達事起，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When the affair of Chen Xianda arose, he was given the additional title General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair of Chen Xianda arose, he was given the additional title general who supports the state.

sentences.zh: 雖用護軍崔慧景為都督，而兵權實在世檦，當時權勢傾法珍、蟲兒。

translations.literal: Although Cui Huijing the Protector of the Army was employed as commander-in-chief, military authority actually rested with Shibiao, whose power at the time eclipsed Fazhen and Chonge.
translations.idiomatic: Although Cui Huijing the Protector of the Army was employed as commander-in-chief, military authority actually rested with Shibiao, whose power at the time eclipsed Fazhen and Chonge.

sentences.zh: 又謂法珍、蟲兒曰：「何世天子無要人，但阿儂貨主惡耳。」

translations.literal: He also said to Fazhen and Chonge: "What age's Son of Heaven lacks trusted men? It is only that you two are detestable masters of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Fazhen and Chonge: "What age's Son of Heaven lacks trusted men? It is only that you two are detestable hoarders of wealth.

sentences.zh: 法珍等與之爭權，遂以白帝，帝稍惡其凶強。

translations.literal: Fazhen and the others competed with him for power and reported him to the emperor; the emperor gradually came to dislike his fierce brutality.
translations.idiomatic: Fazhen and the others competed with him for power and reported him to the emperor; the emperor gradually came to dislike his fierce brutality.

sentences.zh: 世檦竊欲生心，左右徐僧重密知之，發其事，收得千餘人仗及咒詛文，又畫帝十餘形像，備為刑斬刻射支解之狀；

translations.literal: Shibiao secretly harbored rebellious intent; his attendant Xu Sengzhong learned of it in secret and exposed the affair. They seized more than a thousand weapons and curse texts, and painted more than ten images of the emperor, complete with scenes of execution by beheading, carving, shooting, and dismemberment;
translations.idiomatic: Shibiao secretly harbored rebellious intent; his attendant Xu Sengzhong learned of it in secret and exposed the affair. They seized more than a thousand weapons and curse texts, and painted more than ten images of the emperor, complete with scenes of execution by beheading, carving, shooting, and dismemberment;

sentences.zh: 而自作己像著通天冠袞服，題雲徐氏皇帝。

translations.literal: and he had made his own image wearing the sky-piercing cap and imperial robes, inscribed "Emperor of the Xu clan."
translations.idiomatic: and he had made his own image wearing the sky-piercing cap and imperial robes, inscribed "Emperor of the Xu clan."

sentences.zh: 永元二年事發，乃族之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan the affair was exposed, and his entire clan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongyuan the affair was exposed, and his entire clan was executed.

sentences.zh: 自是法珍、蟲兒並為外監，口稱詔敕，中書舍人王咺之與相唇齒，專掌文翰。

translations.literal: From this time Fazhen and Chonge both became outer directors, speaking in the name of imperial edicts; Secretariat attendant Wang Yaozhi worked with them like lip and teeth, holding exclusive charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: From this time Fazhen and Chonge both became outer directors, speaking in the name of imperial edicts; Secretariat attendant Wang Yaozhi worked with them like lip and teeth, holding exclusive charge of documents.

sentences.zh: 其餘二十餘人，皆有勢力。

translations.literal: The remaining more than twenty men all had their share of power.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining more than twenty men all had their share of power.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景平後，法珍封餘幹縣男，蟲兒封竟陵縣男。

translations.literal: After Cui Huijing was put down, Fazhen was enfeoffed as Baron of Yugan county and Chonge as Baron of Jingling county.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Huijing was put down, Fazhen was enfeoffed as baron of Yugan county and Chonge as baron of Jingling county.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景之平，曲赦都下及南兗州，本以宥賊黨，而群凶用事，刑辟不依詔書。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing was suppressed, a partial amnesty was granted for the capital region and South Yanzhou, originally intended to spare the rebel faction—but the pack of villains held power, and punishments did not follow the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Huijing was suppressed, a partial amnesty was granted for the capital region and South Yanzhou, originally intended to spare the rebel faction—but the pack of villains held power, and punishments did not follow the edict.

sentences.zh: 無罪家富者，不論赦令，莫不受戮，籍其家產；

translations.literal: Those without guilt but with wealthy families were killed regardless of the amnesty, without exception, and their households' property was confiscated;
translations.idiomatic: Those without guilt but with wealthy families were killed regardless of the amnesty, without exception, and their households' property was confiscated;

sentences.zh: 與慧景深相關為盡力而家貧者，一無所問。

translations.literal: while those who had worked hard for Huijing but were poor were left alone entirely.
translations.idiomatic: while those who had worked hard for Huijing but were poor were left alone entirely.

sentences.zh: 始安、顯達時亦已如此，至慧景平復然。

translations.literal: It had already been this way during the affairs of Shi'an and Xianda; when Huijing was put down it was the same again.
translations.idiomatic: It had already been this way during the affairs of Shi'an and Xianda; when Huijing was put down it was the same again.

sentences.zh: 或說王咺之云：「赦書無信，人情大惡。」

translations.literal: Someone told Wang Yaozhi: "The amnesty edicts carry no credibility—popular feeling is deeply hostile.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Wang Yaozhi: "The amnesty edicts carry no credibility—popular feeling is deeply hostile.

sentences.zh: 咺之曰：「政當復有赦耳。」

translations.literal: Yaozhi said: "We need only issue another amnesty, that's all."
translations.idiomatic: Yaozhi said: "We need only issue another amnesty, that's all."

sentences.zh: 復赦，群小誅戮亦復如先。

translations.literal: Another amnesty was issued, and the pack of petty villains slaughtered people just as before.
translations.idiomatic: Another amnesty was issued, and the pack of petty villains slaughtered people just as before.

sentences.zh: 帝自群公誅後，無復忌憚，無日不遊走。

translations.literal: Since the senior nobles were executed, the emperor no longer had any restraining fear and went abroad every day without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Since the senior nobles were executed, the emperor no longer had any restraining fear and went abroad every day without fail.

sentences.zh: 所幸潘妃本姓俞名尼子，王敬則伎也。

translations.literal: His favorite, Consort Pan, was originally surnamed Yu and named Nizi; she had been an entertainer of Wang Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: His favorite, Consort Pan, was originally surnamed Yu and named Nizi; she had been an entertainer of Wang Jingze.

sentences.zh: 或云宋文帝有潘妃，在位三十年，於是改姓曰潘，其父寶慶亦從改焉。

translations.literal: Some said Emperor Wen of Song had had a Consort Pan who remained in favor for thirty years—therefore she changed her surname to Pan, and her father Baoqing changed with her.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Emperor Wen of Song had had a Consort Pan who remained in favor for thirty years—therefore she changed her surname to Pan, and her father Baoqing changed with her.

sentences.zh: 帝呼寶慶及法珍為阿丈，蟲兒及東冶營兵俞靈韻為阿兄。

translations.literal: The emperor called Baoqing and Fazhen "Uncle," and Chonge and Yu Lingyun, a soldier of the Eastern Foundry camp, "Elder Brother."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Baoqing and Fazhen "Uncle," and Chonge and Yu Lingyun, a soldier of the Eastern Foundry camp, "Elder Brother."

sentences.zh: 帝與法珍等俱詣寶慶，帝躬自汲水，助廚人作膳，為市中雜語以為諧謔。

translations.literal: The emperor went with Fazhen and the others to visit Baoqing; he personally drew water and helped the kitchen staff prepare food, turning marketplace slang into ribald jokes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went with Fazhen and the others to visit Baoqing; he personally drew water and helped the kitchen staff prepare food, turning marketplace slang into ribald jokes.

sentences.zh: 又帝輕騎戎服往諸刀敕家遊宴，有吉凶輒往慶吊。

translations.literal: The emperor also went in light cavalry and military dress to feast at the homes of the blade-edicts, and whenever there was joy or mourning he would go to congratulate or condole.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also went in light cavalry and military dress to feast at the homes of the blade-edicts, and whenever there was joy or mourning he would go to congratulate or condole.

sentences.zh: 奄人王寶孫年十三四，號為倀子，最有寵，參預朝政，雖王咺之、蟲兒之徒亦下之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Baosun, thirteen or fourteen years old, was called "the heir-son" and was most favored; he participated in court politics, and even men like Wang Yaozhi and Chonge deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Baosun, thirteen or fourteen years old, was called "the heir-son" and was most favored; he participated in court politics, and even men like Wang Yaozhi and Chonge deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 控制大臣，移易敕詔，乃至騎馬入殿，詆訶天子。

translations.literal: He controlled the senior ministers, altered edicts and decrees, and even rode a horse into the hall and reviled the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He controlled the senior ministers, altered edicts and decrees, and even rode a horse into the hall and reviled the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 公卿見之，莫不懾息。

translations.literal: When the nobles and ministers saw him, none failed to shrink back in fear.
translations.idiomatic: When the nobles and ministers saw him, none failed to shrink back in fear.

sentences.zh: 其佐成昏亂者：法珍、蟲兒及王咺之、俞寶慶、俞靈韻、祝靈勇、範亮之、徐僧重、時崇濟、芮安泰、劉文泰、呂文慶、胡輝光、繆買養、章道之、楊敬子、李粲之、周管之、範曇濟、石曇悅、張惡奴、王勝公、王懷藻、梅師濟、鄒伯兒、史元益、王靈范、席休文、解滂及太史令駱文叔、大巫朱光尚，凡三十一人。

translations.literal: Those who assisted in bringing about the chaos: Fazhen, Chonge, and Wang Yaozhi, Yu Baoqing, Yu Lingyun, Zhu Lingyong, Fan Liangzhi, Xu Sengzhong, Shi Chongji, Rui Antai, Liu Wentai, Lü Wenqing, Hu Huiguang, Miao Maiyang, Zhang Daozhi, Yang Jingzi, Li Canzhi, Zhou Guanzhi, Fan Tanji, Shi Tuanyue, Zhang Enu, Wang Shenggong, Wang Huaizao, Mei Shiji, Zou Bo'er, Shi Yuanyi, Wang Lingfan, Xi Xiuwen, Xie Pang, and Grand Astrologer Luo Wenshu, chief shaman Zhu Guangshang—thirty-one in all.
translations.idiomatic: Those who assisted in bringing about the chaos: Fazhen, Chonge, and Wang Yaozhi, Yu Baoqing, Yu Lingyun, Zhu Lingyong, Fan Liangzhi, Xu Sengzhong, Shi Chongji, Rui Antai, Liu Wentai, Lü Wenqing, Hu Huiguang, Miao Maiyang, Zhang Daozhi, Yang Jingzi, Li Canzhi, Zhou Guanzhi, Fan Tanji, Shi Tuanyue, Zhang Enu, Wang Shenggong, Wang Huaizao, Mei Shiji, Zou Bo'er, Shi Yuanyi, Wang Lingfan, Xi Xiuwen, Xie Pang, and Grand Astrologer Luo Wenshu, chief shaman Zhu Guangshang—thirty-one in all.

sentences.zh: 又有奄官王寶孫、王法昭、許朗之、許伯孫、方佛念、馬僧猛、盛劭、王竺兒、隨要、袁系世等十人。

translations.literal: There were also ten eunuch officials: Wang Baosun, Wang Fazhao, Xu Langzhi, Xu Bosun, Fang Fonian, Ma Sengmeng, Sheng Shao, Wang Zhu'er, Sui Yao, and Yuan Shishi.
translations.idiomatic: There were also ten eunuch officials: Wang Baosun, Wang Fazhao, Xu Langzhi, Xu Bosun, Fang Fonian, Ma Sengmeng, Sheng Shao, Wang Zhu'er, Sui Yao, and Yuan Shishi.

sentences.zh: 梁武平建鄴，皆誅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang pacified Jiankang, all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang pacified Jiankang, all were executed.

sentences.zh: 又朱興光為茹法珍所疾，得罪被系，豐勇之與王珍國相知，行殺皆免。

translations.literal: Also Zhu Xingguang was hated by Ru Fazhen and, having offended, was imprisoned; Feng Yongzhi was acquainted with Wang Zhenguo, and even when executions were ordered, those concerned were always spared.
translations.idiomatic: Also Zhu Xingguang was hated by Ru Fazhen and, having offended, was imprisoned; Feng Yongzhi was acquainted with Wang Zhenguo, and even when executions were ordered, those concerned were always spared.

sentences.zh: 初，左右刀敕之徒悉號為鬼，宮中訛云：「趙鬼食鴨歗，諸鬼盡著調。」

translations.literal: Initially the blade-edicts on the emperor's left and right were all called "ghosts." A rumor in the palace ran: "When Zhao the ghost eats duck xiao, all the ghosts put on costumes.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the blade-edicts on the emperor's left and right were all called "ghosts." A rumor in the palace ran: "When Zhao the ghost eats duck xiao, all the ghosts put on costumes.

sentences.zh: 當時莫解。

translations.literal: At the time no one understood it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time no one understood it.

sentences.zh: 梁武平建鄴，東昏死，群小一時誅滅，故稱為諸鬼也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang pacified Jiankang and Donghun died, the petty villains were wiped out all at once—hence they were called "the ghosts."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang pacified Jiankang and Donghun died, the petty villains were wiped out all at once—hence they were called "the ghosts."

sentences.zh: 俗間以細銼肉糅以姜桂曰歗，意者以凶黨皆當細銼而烹之也。

translations.literal: Among the people, minced meat mixed with ginger and cassia is called xiao; presumably the meaning was that the wicked faction should all be minced fine and boiled.
