translations.idiomatic: Among the people, minced meat mixed with ginger and cassia is called xiao; presumably the meaning was that the wicked faction should all be minced fine and boiled.

sentences.zh: 周石珍

translations.literal: Zhou Shizhen
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shizhen

sentences.zh: 周石珍，建康之塚隸也，世以販絹為業。

translations.literal: Zhou Shizhen was a tomb attendant of Jiankang; his family had sold silk for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shizhen was a tomb attendant of Jiankang; his family had sold silk for generations.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，稍遷至宣傳左右。

translations.literal: During Tianjian of Liang he rose gradually to attendant in the Secretariat for transmission.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianjian of Liang he rose gradually to attendant in the Secretariat for transmission.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺，頗閑應對，後遂至制局監，帶開陽令。

translations.literal: He stood seven feet tall, was quite skilled in repartee, and later reached director of the arsenal bureau, concurrently serving as magistrate of Kaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet tall, was quite skilled in repartee, and later reached director of the arsenal bureau, concurrently serving as magistrate of Kaiyang.

sentences.zh: 歷位直合將軍。

translations.literal: He served in turn as general of the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as general of the Direct Gate.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，封南豐縣侯，猶領制局。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanfeng county and still held the arsenal bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiqing he was enfeoffed as marquis of Nanfeng county and still held the arsenal bureau.

sentences.zh: 台城未陷，已射書與侯景相結，門初開，石珍猶侍左右。

translations.literal: Before the capital garrison fell, he had already sent letters by arrow to Hou Jing to conspire with him; when the gates first opened, Shizhen was still attending at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Before the capital garrison fell, he had already sent letters by arrow to Hou Jing to conspire with him; when the gates first opened, Shizhen was still attending at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 時賊遣其徒入直殿內，或驅驢馬出入殿庭。

translations.literal: At that time the rebels sent their men to stand duty inside the halls, and some drove donkeys and horses in and out of the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebels sent their men to stand duty inside the halls, and some drove donkeys and horses in and out of the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 武帝方坐文德殿，怪問之，石珍曰：「皆丞相甲士。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was just seated in the Hall of Cultured Virtue and asked in wonder; Shizhen said: "They are all the Chancellor's armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was just seated in the Hall of Cultured Virtue and asked in wonder; Shizhen said: "They are all the Chancellor's armored soldiers.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何物丞相？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What Chancellor is this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What Chancellor is this?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「侯丞相。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Chancellor Hou."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Chancellor Hou."

sentences.zh: 上怒叱之曰：「是名侯景，何謂丞相！」

translations.literal: The emperor shouted angrily: "That man's name is Hou Jing—how dare you call him Chancellor!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shouted angrily: "That man's name is Hou Jing—how dare you call him Chancellor!"

sentences.zh: 石珍求媚於賊，乃養其党田遷以為己子，遷亦父事之。

translations.literal: Shizhen sought to fawn on the rebels; he took Tian Qian, a member of their faction, and raised him as his own son, and Qian likewise treated him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen sought to fawn on the rebels; he took Tian Qian, a member of their faction, and raised him as his own son, and Qian likewise treated him as a father.

sentences.zh: 景篡位，制度羽儀皆石珍自出。

translations.literal: When Jing usurped the throne, the regulations for rites and regalia all came from Shizhen himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing usurped the throne, the regulations for rites and regalia all came from Shizhen himself.

sentences.zh: 景平後，及中書舍人嚴亶等送於江陵。

translations.literal: After Jing was suppressed, he and Secretariat attendant Yan Dan and the others were sent to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing was suppressed, he and Secretariat attendant Yan Dan and the others were sent to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 亶本為齋監，居台省積久，多閑故實。

translations.literal: Dan had originally been overseer of the fast hall; having long resided in the capital offices, he was well versed in old precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had originally been overseer of the fast hall; having long resided in the capital offices, he was well versed in old precedents.

sentences.zh: 在賊居要，亞于石珍。

translations.literal: Among the rebels he held an important post, second only to Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Among the rebels he held an important post, second only to Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 及簡文見立，亶學北人著靴上殿，無肅恭之禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jian was established, Dan imitated northerners in wearing boots to enter the hall, without the usual reverent courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jian was established, Dan imitated northerners in wearing boots to enter the hall, without the usual reverent courtesy.

sentences.zh: 有怪之者，亶曰：「吾豈畏劉禪乎。」

translations.literal: When some found this strange, Dan said: "Do you think I fear Liu Shan?
translations.idiomatic: When some found this strange, Dan said: "Do you think I fear Liu Shan?

sentences.zh: 從景圍巴陵郡，叫曰：「荊州那不送降！」

translations.literal: When he followed Jing in besieging Baling commandery, he shouted: "Why doesn't Jingzhou send word to surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Jing in besieging Baling commandery, he shouted: "Why doesn't Jingzhou send word to surrender!"

sentences.zh: 及至江陵，將刑於市，泣謂石珍曰：「吾等死亦是罪盈。」

translations.literal: When he reached Jiangling and was about to be executed in the marketplace, he wept and said to Shizhen: "Our deaths are only what overflowing guilt deserves."
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Jiangling and was about to be executed in the marketplace, he wept and said to Shizhen: "Our deaths are only what overflowing guilt deserves."

sentences.zh: 石珍與其子升相抱哭。

translations.literal: Shizhen and his son Sheng embraced each other and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen and his son Sheng embraced each other and wept.

sentences.zh: 亶謂監刑人曰：「倩語湘東王，不有廢也，君何以興？」

translations.literal: Dan said to the executioner: "Please tell the Prince of Xiangdong: had there been no deposition, how could you have risen?
translations.idiomatic: Dan said to the executioner: "Please tell the Prince of Xiangdong: had there been no deposition, how could you have risen?

sentences.zh: 俱腰斬。

translations.literal: Both were cut in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Both were cut in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 自是更殺賊黨，以板柙舌，釘釘之，不復得語。

translations.literal: From this time onward, when rebel partisans were executed further, their tongues were clamped with boards and nailed so they could no longer speak.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward, when rebel partisans were executed further, their tongues were clamped with boards and nailed so they could no longer speak.

sentences.zh: 陸驗、徐驎，並吳郡吳人。

translations.literal: Lu Yan and Xu Lin were both natives of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan and Xu Lin were both natives of Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 驗少而貧苦，落魄無行。

translations.literal: Yan was poor and wretched from youth, dissolute and without propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was poor and wretched from youth, dissolute and without propriety.

sentences.zh: 邑人郁吉卿者甚富，驗傾身事之。

translations.literal: A townsman named Yu Jiqing was very rich, and Yan devoted himself entirely to serving him.
translations.idiomatic: A townsman named Yu Jiqing was very rich, and Yan devoted himself entirely to serving him.

sentences.zh: 吉卿貸以錢米，驗藉以商販，遂致千金。

translations.literal: Jiqing lent him money and grain; Yan used these for trade and eventually amassed a thousand gold.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing lent him money and grain; Yan used these for trade and eventually amassed a thousand gold.

sentences.zh: 因出都下，散貲以事權貴。

translations.literal: He then went to the capital and spread his wealth to cultivate the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to the capital and spread his wealth to cultivate the powerful.

sentences.zh: 朱異，其邑子也，故嘗有德，遂言于武帝拔之，與徐驎兩人遞為少府丞、太市令。

translations.literal: Zhu Yi was a fellow townsman, and Yan had once done him a kindness; Yi therefore spoke to Emperor Wu and had him promoted, and he and Xu Lin alternated as vice director of the Ministry of the Privy Purse and market director.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi was a fellow townsman, and Yan had once done him a kindness; Yi therefore spoke to Emperor Wu and had him promoted, and he and Xu Lin alternated as vice director of the Ministry of the Privy Purse and market director.

sentences.zh: 驗本無藝業，而容貌特醜。

translations.literal: Yan had no real accomplishment to speak of, and his appearance was exceptionally ugly.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had no real accomplishment to speak of, and his appearance was exceptionally ugly.

sentences.zh: 先是，外國獻生犀，其形甚陋，故閭里咸謂驗為生犀。

translations.literal: Earlier, a foreign state had presented a living rhinoceros whose form was very ugly, so people in the lanes all called Yan "the living rhinoceros."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a foreign state had presented a living rhinoceros whose form was very ugly, so people in the lanes all called Yan "the living rhinoceros."

sentences.zh: 驗、驎並以苛刻為務，百賈畏之，異尤與之昵，世人謂之三蠹。

translations.literal: Yan and Lin both made harsh exaction their business; all merchants feared them, and Yi was especially intimate with them—people called them the Three Vermin.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Lin both made harsh exaction their business; all merchants feared them, and Yi was especially intimate with them—people called them the Three Vermin.

sentences.zh: 司農卿傅岐，梗直士也，嘗謂異曰：「卿任參國鈞，榮寵如此，比日所聞，鄙穢狼藉，若使聖主發悟，欲免得乎？」

translations.literal: Minister of Finance Fu Qi was an upright man; he once said to Yi: "You share in governing the realm and enjoy such glory and favor—yet what I have heard these days is base and filthy beyond measure. If our sage sovereign awakens to it, do you think you can escape punishment?
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Finance Fu Qi was an upright man; he once said to Yi: "You share in governing the realm and enjoy such glory and favor—yet what I have heard these days is base and filthy beyond measure. If our sage sovereign awakens to it, do you think you can escape punishment?

sentences.zh: 異曰：「外間謗讟，知之久矣，心苟無媿，何恤人言。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "The slander outside I have known for a long time; if the heart is without guilt, why fear what people say?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said: "The slander outside I have known for a long time; if the heart is without guilt, why fear what people say?"

sentences.zh: 岐謂人曰：「朱彥和將死矣，恃諂以求容，肆辯以拒諫，聞難而不懼，知惡而不改。

translations.literal: Qi said to others: "Zhu Yanhe is about to die—relying on flattery to win favor, unleashing argument to reject remonstrance, hearing hardship without fear, knowing wickedness without reform.
translations.idiomatic: Qi said to others: "Zhu Yanhe is about to die—relying on flattery to win favor, unleashing argument to reject remonstrance, hearing hardship without fear, knowing wickedness without reform.

sentences.zh: 天奪其鑒，其能久乎。」

translations.literal: Heaven has taken away his mirror of judgment; how much longer can he endure?"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has stripped him of discernment—how much longer can he last?"

sentences.zh: 驗竟以侵削為能，數年遂登列棘，鳴佩珥貂，並肩英彥。

translations.literal: Yan nevertheless made exaction and squeezing his specialty; within a few years he rose to a post at the Censorate, his pendant sounding and mink tails at his cap, standing shoulder to shoulder with outstanding men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yan made harsh exaction his trade; within a few years he had risen to a seat at the Censorate, pendant chiming and mink tails at his cap, standing shoulder to shoulder with the finest men of the day.

sentences.zh: 仕至太子右衛率，卒，贈右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He served as Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Right Guard; when he died he was posthumously awarded the title General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Right Guard and, upon his death, was posthumously made General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 遠近聞其死，莫不快之。

translations.literal: Near and far, when they heard of his death, none failed to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far, when word of his death spread, everyone rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 驎素為邵陵王綸所憾，太清二年，為綸所殺。

translations.literal: Lin had long been resented by the Prince of Shaoling, Wang Lun; in the second year of Taiqing he was killed by Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had long been an object of resentment to the Prince of Shaoling, Wang Lun; in the second year of Taiqing, Lun had him killed.

sentences.zh: 司馬申

translations.literal: Sima Shen
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shen

sentences.zh: 司馬申，字季和，河內溫人也。

translations.literal: Sima Shen, courtesy name Jihe, was a native of Wen in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shen, styled Jihe, was a native of Wen in Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖慧遠，梁都水使者。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huiyuan was Commissioner of Waterways under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huiyuan served Liang as Commissioner of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 父玄通，梁尚書左戶郎。

translations.literal: His father Xuantong was Left Section Clerk in the Ministry of Revenue under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuantong was Left Section Clerk in the Ministry of Revenue under Liang.

sentences.zh: 申早有風鑒，十四便善弈棋。

translations.literal: Shen early showed discernment; at fourteen he was already skilled at weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen showed keen judgment from youth; by fourteen he was already an accomplished player of weiqi.

sentences.zh: 嘗隨父候吏部尚書到溉，時梁州刺史陰子春、領軍朱異在焉，呼與棋。

translations.literal: Once he accompanied his father to call on Dao Gai, Director of the Ministry of Civil Appointments; Yin Zichun, Inspector of Liang province, and Zhu Yi, Director of the Central Secretariat, were present, and they called the boy to play.
translations.idiomatic: Once he went with his father to visit Dao Gai, Director of the Ministry of Civil Appointments; Yin Zichun, Inspector of Liang province, and Zhu Yi, Director of the Central Secretariat, were there, and they summoned him to play.

sentences.zh: 申每有妙思，異觀而奇之，因引申遊處。

translations.literal: Whenever Shen produced a fine stroke of inspiration, Yi watched and marvelled at it, and thereafter invited Shen to join him on outings.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shen made a brilliant move, Yi watched in wonder and thereafter took him along on his outings.

sentences.zh: 太清之難，父母俱沒，因此自誓，擔土菜食終身。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Taiqing both his parents perished; because of this he vowed to himself to carry earth upon his shoulders and eat vegetables alone for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the catastrophe of Taiqing both his parents died; he then vowed to carry earth on his shoulders and eat plain vegetables for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承制，累遷鎮西外兵記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the regency, Shen was repeatedly promoted, eventually becoming Recorder on the Staff of the General Who Guards the West for External Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed provisional authority, Shen rose through repeated promotions to Recorder on the staff of the General Who Guards the West for external military affairs.

sentences.zh: 及侯景寇郢州，申隨都督王僧辯據巴陵，每進策，皆見行用。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing attacked Yingzhou, Shen followed the commander Wang Sengbian in holding Baling; every plan he submitted was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing raided Yingzhou, Shen followed the commander Wang Sengbian in holding Baling; every plan he offered was put into practice.

sentences.zh: 僧辯歎曰：「此生要鞬汗馬，或非所長，若使撫眾守城，必有奇績。」

translations.literal: Sengbian sighed and said: "If this man's forte is drawing bow and sweating horses, that may not be his strength; but give him command of men defending a city, and he will surely achieve remarkable deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian sighed and said, "If this man's gift lies in drawing bow and sweating the horse, that may not be his strength; but put him in charge of men defending a city, and he will surely achieve remarkable feats.

sentences.zh: 僧辯之討陸納也，于時賊眾奄至，左右披靡，申躬蔽僧辯，蒙楯而前，會裴之橫救至，賊乃退。

translations.literal: When Sengbian marched to suppress Lu Na, the rebel host suddenly arrived and his attendants scattered; Shen threw his body before Sengbian, advancing under shield; just then Pei Zhiheng's relief arrived and the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian marched against Lu Na, the rebel host suddenly appeared and his attendants broke and fled; Shen shielded Sengbian with his own body and advanced under cover of his shield. Pei Zhiheng's relief force arrived in time, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 僧辯顧而笑曰：「仁者必有勇，豈虛言哉。」

translations.literal: Sengbian turned and smiled: "The benevolent man is always brave—was that an empty saying after all?"
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian turned and smiled. "The benevolent man is always brave—those were no empty words after all."

sentences.zh: 陳太建中，除秣陵令，在職以清能見紀，有白雀集於縣庭。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era of Chen he was appointed Magistrate of Moling; in office he was noted for integrity and ability, and a white finch alighted in the courtyard of the magistracy.
translations.idiomatic: During Chen's Taikang era he was appointed magistrate of Moling; in office he won notice for integrity and competence, and a white finch alighted in the courtyard of the county seat.

sentences.zh: 復為東宮通事舍人。

translations.literal: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Master of Ceremonies of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Master of Ceremonies of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 叔陵之肆逆也，事既不捷，出據東府，申馳召右衛將軍蕭摩訶帥兵先至，追斬之，後主深嘉焉。

translations.literal: When Shuling launched his treason and the affair did not succeed, he withdrew to hold the Eastern Palace; Shen galloped off to summon General of the Right Guard Xiao Mohe to lead troops there first, pursued Shuling, and cut him down; the Later Lord was deeply pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuling launched his rebellion and the attempt failed, he withdrew to hold the Eastern Palace. Shen galloped to summon General of the Right Guard Xiao Mohe, who led troops there first, pursued Shuling, and cut him down; the Later Lord was deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 以功除太子左衛率，封文招縣伯，兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: For this merit he was appointed Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Left Guard, enfeoffed as Baron of Wenzhao County, and given the additional post of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Master of Ceremonies of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Left Guard, enfeoffed as Baron of Wenzhao county, and given the additional post of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Master of Ceremonies of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 曆事三帝，內掌機密，頗作威福。

translations.literal: Having served three emperors, he handled confidential affairs within the palace and wielded considerable power for his own benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Having served three emperors, he controlled confidential affairs within the palace and wielded no small power for his own advantage.

sentences.zh: 性忍害，好飛書以譖毀，朝之端士，遍罹其殃。

translations.literal: Cruel by nature, he loved to send anonymous letters of accusation; upright gentlemen throughout the court fell victim to him one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Cruel by nature, he loved to dispatch anonymous letters of denunciation; upright men throughout the court fell victim to him one after another.

sentences.zh: 參預謀謨，乃于外宣說，以為己力，省中秘事，往往洩漏。

translations.literal: He took part in deliberations on strategy, then proclaimed them outside as his own achievement; confidential business of the Secretariat was constantly leaking out.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in strategic deliberations, then proclaimed them abroad as his own doing; confidential business of the Secretariat constantly leaked out.

sentences.zh: 性又果敢，善應對，能候人主顏色。

translations.literal: He was also bold and quick in reply, skilled at reading the sovereign's expression.
translations.idiomatic: He was also bold and quick in reply, skilled at reading the sovereign's mood.

sentences.zh: 有忤己者，必以微言譖之；

translations.literal: Anyone who crossed him he was sure to slander with insinuating words;
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who crossed him he was sure to slander with insinuating words;

sentences.zh: 附己者，因機進之。

translations.literal: those who sided with him he advanced when opportunity arose.
translations.idiomatic: those who sided with him he advanced when opportunity arose.

sentences.zh: 是以朝廷內外，皆從風靡。

translations.literal: Thus within and without the court, all bowed to his wind.
translations.idiomatic: Thus within and without the court, all bowed before his influence.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書右僕射沈君理卒，朝廷議以毛喜代之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Vice Director of the Secretariat Shen Junli had died, and the court deliberated appointing Mao Xi in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Vice Director of the Secretariat Shen Junli had died, and the court deliberated appointing Mao Xi to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 申慮喜預政，乃短喜於後主曰：「喜臣之妻兄，高帝時稱陛下有酒德，請逐去宮臣，陛下甯忘之邪！」

translations.literal: Shen feared that if Xi entered government he would lose influence, and so he spoke ill of Xi to the Later Lord: "Xi is my wife's elder brother. In Emperor Gao's day he said Your Majesty had 'the virtue of wine' and asked to drive away the palace attendants—surely Your Majesty has not forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: Shen feared that if Xi entered government his own influence would suffer, and so he spoke ill of Xi to the Later Lord: "Xi is my wife's elder brother. In Emperor Gao's day he praised Your Majesty's 'virtue in wine' and asked to drive away the palace attendants—surely Your Majesty has not forgotten?

sentences.zh: 喜由是廢錮。

translations.literal: Xi was therefore removed from office and placed under house arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was therefore dismissed from office and placed under house arrest.

sentences.zh: 又與施文慶、李脫兒比周，譖殺傅縡，奪任忠部曲以配蔡征、孔範，是以文武解體，至於覆滅。

translations.literal: He also colluded with Shi Wenqing and Li Tuo'er, slandered and killed Fu Xie, and stripped Ren Zhong of his personal troops to assign them to Cai Zheng and Kong Fan—in consequence the military and civil service collapsed, leading all the way to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: He also colluded with Shi Wenqing and Li Tuo'er, slandered and killed Fu Xie, and stripped Ren Zhong of his personal troops to assign them to Cai Zheng and Kong Fan—in consequence the military and civil service fell apart, all the way to the dynasty's ruin.

sentences.zh: 申嘗晝寢于尚書下省，有烏啄其口，流血及地，時論以為譖賢之效也。

translations.literal: Once Shen was napping by day in the Secretariat's lower offices when a bird pecked his mouth until blood ran to the ground; public opinion took this as the effect of slandering worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shen was napping by day in the lower offices of the Secretariat when a bird pecked his mouth until blood ran to the ground; public opinion took this as retribution for slandering worthy men.

sentences.zh: 後加散騎常侍，右衛、舍人如故。

translations.literal: Later he was additionally made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary; his posts as General of the Right Guard and Attendant-in-Ordinary remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was additionally made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary; his posts as General of the Right Guard and Attendant-in-Ordinary remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 至德四年卒，後主嗟悼久之。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Zhide; the Later Lord mourned him at length.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Zhide, and the Later Lord mourned him at length.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、護軍將軍，進爵為侯，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Attendant-in-Chief and General Who Protects the Army, advanced in rank to Marquis, and given the posthumous epithet Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Attendant-in-Chief and General Who Protects the Army, advanced in rank to marquis, and given the posthumous epithet Loyal.

sentences.zh: 及葬，後主自為制志銘。

translations.literal: At his burial the Later Lord himself composed the inscription for his stele and record.
translations.idiomatic: At his burial the Later Lord himself composed the epitaph.

sentences.zh: 子琇嗣，官至太子舍人。

translations.literal: His son Xiu succeeded him and rose to Attendant of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiu succeeded him and rose to Attendant of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 施文慶

translations.literal: Shi Wenqing
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wenqing

sentences.zh: 禎明三年，湘州刺史晉熙王叔文在職既久，大得人和，後主以其據有上流，陰忌之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming, Wang Shuwen, Prince of Jinxi, had long held the post of Inspector of Xiangzhou and had won great harmony among the people; the Later Lord secretly resented him because he held the upper Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenming, Wang Shuwen, Prince of Jinxi, had long served as Inspector of Xiangzhou and had won great goodwill among the people; the Later Lord secretly resented him because he held the upper Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 自度素與群臣少恩，恐不為用，無所任者，乃擢文慶為都督、湘州刺史，配以精兵，欲令西上，仍征叔文還朝。

translations.literal: The Later Lord reckoned that he had never shown much kindness to his ministers and feared he could not rely on them; finding no one fit for the task, he promoted Wenqing to Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Xiangzhou, assigning him picked troops, intending to send him west while summoning Shuwen back to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord reckoned that he had never shown his ministers much favor and feared he could not rely on them; finding no one else fit for the task, he promoted Wenqing to Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Xiangzhou, assigning him picked troops, intending to send him west while summoning Shuwen back to court.

sentences.zh: 文慶深喜其事，然懼居外，後執事者持己短長，因進其党沈客卿以自代。

translations.literal: Wenqing was overjoyed at the appointment, yet he feared that if he left the capital those in power would seize on his faults; he therefore recommended his ally Shen Keqing to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing was delighted by the appointment, yet he feared that once he was abroad those in power would seize on his faults; he therefore recommended his ally Shen Keqing to replace him.

sentences.zh: 未發間，二人共掌機密。

translations.literal: Before Wenqing set out, the two men jointly controlled confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wenqing set out, the two men jointly controlled confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 時隋軍大舉，分道而進，尚書僕射袁憲、驃騎將軍蕭摩訶及文武群臣共議，請於京口、採石各置兵五千，並出金翅二百，緣江上下，以為防備。

translations.literal: At that time the Sui armies were advancing in strength along several routes; Vice Director of the Secretariat Yuan Xian, Cavalry General Xiao Mohe, and civil and military ministers jointly urged that five thousand troops be posted at Jingkou and Caishi respectively, and two hundred Golden Wings be sent up and down the river as a defensive measure.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Sui armies were advancing in force along several routes; Vice Director Yuan Xian, Cavalry General Xiao Mohe, and civil and military ministers jointly urged that five thousand troops be posted at Jingkou and Caishi respectively, and two hundred Golden Wings be sent up and down the river as a defensive measure.

sentences.zh: 文慶恐無兵從己，廢其述職，而客卿又利文慶之任己得專權，俱言於朝曰：「必有論議，不假面陳，但作文啟，即為通奏。」

translations.literal: Wenqing feared that if troops were deployed he would have none to follow him and would lose his chance to take up his post; Keqing also wanted Wenqing to go so that he himself could monopolize power; together they told the court: "There will certainly be debate; there is no need to state the case in person—simply write a memorial and it will be forwarded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing feared that if troops were deployed he would have none to follow him and would lose his chance to take up his post; Keqing also wanted Wenqing to go so that he himself could monopolize power; together they told the court, "There will certainly be debate; there is no need to state the case in person—simply write a memorial and it will be forwarded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 憲等以為然。

translations.literal: Xian and the others agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xian and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 二人齎啟入白後主曰：「此是常事，邊城將帥，足以當之。

translations.literal: The two men carried in their memorial and reported to the Later Lord: "This is an ordinary matter; the border commanders are quite sufficient to deal with it.
translations.idiomatic: The two men carried in their memorial and reported to the Later Lord, "This is an ordinary matter; the frontier commanders are quite sufficient to deal with it.

sentences.zh: 若出人船，必恐驚擾。」

translations.literal: If we dispatch troops and ships, we shall only cause alarm and disturbance."
translations.idiomatic: If we dispatch troops and ships, we shall only cause alarm and disturbance."

sentences.zh: 及隋軍臨江，間諜驟至，憲等殷懃奏請，至於再三。

translations.literal: When the Sui armies reached the river, spies arrived one after another, and Xian and the others repeatedly and urgently petitioned—again and again.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui armies reached the river, spies arrived in rapid succession, and Xian and the others urgently petitioned again and again.

sentences.zh: 文慶等曰：「元會將逼，南郊之日，太子多從，今若出兵，事便廢闕。」

translations.literal: Wenqing and the others said: "The New Year's audience is imminent, and on the day of the southern suburban sacrifice the crown prince will follow in great number; if troops are sent out now the rites will have to be cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing and the others said, "The New Year's audience is imminent, and on the day of the southern suburban sacrifice the crown prince will follow in great number; if troops are sent out now the rites will have to be cancelled.

sentences.zh: 後主曰：「今且出兵，若北邊無事，因以水軍從郊，何為不可。」

translations.literal: The Later Lord said: "Deploy troops for now; if nothing happens on the northern front, the fleet can still follow the sacrifice—why not?"
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord said, "Deploy troops for now; if nothing happens on the northern front, the fleet can still follow the sacrifice—why not?"

sentences.zh: 又對曰：「如此，則聲聞鄰境，便謂國弱。」

translations.literal: They replied again: "In that case the news will reach neighboring states and they will say the country is weak."
translations.idiomatic: They replied again, "In that case the news will reach neighboring states and they will say the country is weak."

sentences.zh: 後又以貨動江總，總內為之遊說，後主重違其意，而迫群官之請，乃令付外詳議，又抑憲等，由是未決，而隋師濟江。

translations.literal: Later they also bribed Jiang Zong, who lobbied on their behalf from within; the Later Lord was loath to go against him, yet pressed by the ministers' petitions, he ordered the matter referred for detailed deliberation outside and again checked Yuan Xian and the others—thus nothing was decided, and the Sui troops crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Later they also bribed Jiang Zong, who lobbied on their behalf from within; the Later Lord was loath to go against him, yet pressed by the ministers' petitions, he ordered the matter referred for detailed deliberation outside and again checked Yuan Xian and the others—thus nothing was decided, and the Sui troops crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 後主性怯懦，不達軍事，晝夜啼泣，台內處分，一以委之。

translations.literal: The Later Lord was timid by nature and knew nothing of military affairs; he wept day and night, and all decisions within the palace he entrusted entirely to Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord was timid by nature and knew nothing of military affairs; he wept day and night, and entrusted all decisions within the palace entirely to Wenqing.

sentences.zh: 文慶既知諸將疾己，恐其有功，乃奏曰：「此等怏怏，素不服官，迫此事機，那可專信。」

translations.literal: Wenqing, knowing the generals resented him and fearing they might win merit, memorialized: "These men are discontented and have never respected authority; at this crisis how can we trust them alone?
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing, knowing the generals resented him and fearing they might win merit, memorialized, "These men are discontented and have never respected authority; at this crisis how can we trust them alone?

sentences.zh: 凡有所啟請，經略之計，並皆不行。

translations.literal: Whatever petitions or strategic plans were submitted, none were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever petitions or strategic plans were submitted, none were carried out.

sentences.zh: 尋敕文慶領兵頓于樂游苑。

translations.literal: Soon Wenqing was ordered to lead troops and encamp at Leyou Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wenqing was ordered to lead troops and encamp at Leyou Garden.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，隋晉王廣以文慶受委不忠，曲為諂佞，以蔽耳目，比黨數人，並于石闕前斬之，以謝百姓。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, Prince Jin of Sui, Yang Guang, condemned Wenqing for accepting trust without loyalty, twisting truth to flatter and deceive, and blinding the sovereign's ears; Wenqing and several of his faction were beheaded before the Stone Gate to appease the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, Sui's Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, condemned Wenqing for accepting trust without loyalty, twisting truth to flatter and deceive, and blinding the sovereign's ears; Wenqing and several of his faction were beheaded before the Stone Gate to appease the people.

sentences.zh: 沈客卿

translations.literal: Shen Keqing
translations.idiomatic: Shen Keqing

sentences.zh: 沈客卿，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Keqing was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Keqing was a native of Wukang in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 美風采，善談論，博涉群書，與施文慶少相親昵。

translations.literal: Handsome in bearing, skilled in discourse, widely read in many books, he had been close to Shi Wenqing from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in bearing, skilled in discourse, and widely read, he had been close to Shi Wenqing from youth.

sentences.zh: 仕陳，累遷至尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: Under Chen he rose through repeated promotion to Director of the Ceremonial Section in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen he rose through repeated promotions to Director of the Ceremonial Section in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 聰明有口辯，頗知故事。

translations.literal: Clever and eloquent, he knew precedent well.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and eloquent, he knew precedent well.

sentences.zh: 每朝廷體式，吉凶儀注，凡所疑議，客卿斟酌裁斷，理雖有不經，而眾莫能屈，事多施行。

translations.literal: Whenever court ritual, auspicious and inauspicious observances, or any doubtful point of ceremony arose, Keqing would weigh and decide it; though his reasoning sometimes departed from established practice, none could refute him, and his decisions were largely adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever court ritual, auspicious and inauspicious observances, or any doubtful point of ceremony arose, Keqing would weigh and decide it; though his reasoning sometimes departed from established practice, none could refute him, and his decisions were largely adopted.

sentences.zh: 至德初，以為中書舍人，兼步兵校尉，掌金帛局。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide he was made Attendant of the Secretariat, with the additional rank of Commandant of Footsoldiers, and placed in charge of the Gold and Silk Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhide he was made Attendant of the Secretariat, with the additional rank of Commandant of Footsoldiers, and placed in charge of the Gold and Silk Bureau.

sentences.zh: 以舊制軍人士人，二品清官，並無關市之稅。

translations.literal: By old regulation, military men and literati in the second rank of pure offices were all exempt from market tolls.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation, military men and literati holding second-rank pure offices were all exempt from market tolls.

sentences.zh: 後主盛修宮室，窮極耳目，府庫空虛，有所興造，恒苦不給。

translations.literal: The Later Lord lavishly built palaces, pursuing pleasure to the limit; the treasury stood empty, and whenever he undertook construction he constantly suffered short supply.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord lavishly built palaces, pursuing pleasure to the limit; the treasury stood empty, and whenever he undertook construction he constantly found funds insufficient.

sentences.zh: 客卿每立異端，唯以刻削百姓為事，奏請不問士庶，並責關市之估，而又增重其舊。

translations.literal: Keqing always proposed new schemes, making the squeezing of the people his sole business; he memorialized that commoners and gentry alike should pay market assessments, and on top of that increased the old rates.
translations.idiomatic: Keqing always proposed new schemes, making the squeezing of the people his sole business; he memorialized that commoners and gentry alike should pay market assessments, and on top of that increased the old rates.

sentences.zh: 於是以陽惠朗為太市令，暨慧景為尚書金、倉都令史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yang Huilang was made Director of the Great Market and Ji Huijing was made Chief Clerk of the Gold and Granary Sections in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yang Huilang was made Director of the Great Market and Ji Huijing was made Chief Clerk of the Gold and Granary Sections in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二人家本小吏，考校簿領，豪厘不差，糾謫嚴急，百姓嗟怨。

translations.literal: Both men's families were originally minor clerks; in checking ledgers they missed not the slightest fraction, and their corrections and penalties were severe—the people groaned in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Both men's families were originally minor clerks; in checking ledgers they missed not the slightest fraction, and their corrections and penalties were severe—the people groaned in resentment.

sentences.zh: 而客卿居舍人，總以督之，每歲所入，過於常格數十倍，後主大悅。

translations.literal: Keqing, remaining Attendant of the Secretariat, supervised them in general; each year's receipts exceeded the usual quota many times over, and the Later Lord was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Keqing, remaining Attendant of the Secretariat, supervised them in general; each year's receipts exceeded the usual quota many times over, and the Later Lord was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 尋加客卿散騎常侍、左衛將軍，舍人如故。

translations.literal: Keqing was soon given the additional posts of Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard; his post as Attendant remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Keqing was soon given the additional posts of Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard; his post as Attendant remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 惠朗、慧景奉朝請。

translations.literal: Huilang and Huijing were made Regular Attendants at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Huilang and Huijing were made Regular Attendants at Court.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年，客卿遂與文慶俱掌機密。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming, Keqing came to control confidential affairs together with Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenming, Keqing came to control confidential affairs together with Wenqing.

sentences.zh: 隋師至，文慶出頓樂游苑，內外事客卿總焉。

translations.literal: When the Sui armies arrived, Wenqing went out to encamp at Leyou Garden, and Keqing held authority over all internal and external affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui armies arrived, Wenqing went out to encamp at Leyou Garden, and Keqing held authority over all internal and external affairs.

sentences.zh: 台城失守，隋晉王以客卿重賦厚斂，以悅於上，與文慶、暨慧景、陽惠朗等，俱斬于石闕前。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Prince Jin of Sui condemned Keqing for heavy taxes and harsh exactions to please his sovereign; Keqing, Wenqing, Ji Huijing, Yang Huilang, and others were all beheaded before the Stone Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Sui's Prince of Jin condemned Keqing for heavy taxes and harsh exactions to please his sovereign; Keqing, Wenqing, Ji Huijing, Yang Huilang, and others were all beheaded before the Stone Gate.

sentences.zh: 徐哲，不知何許人，施文慶引為制局監，掌刑法，亦與客卿同誅。

translations.literal: Xu Zhe, of unknown origin, was brought in by Shi Wenqing as Director of the Regulatory Bureau with charge of criminal law; he was executed together with Keqing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhe, of unknown origin, was brought in by Shi Wenqing as Director of the Regulatory Bureau with charge of criminal law; he was executed together with Keqing.

sentences.zh: 孔範字法言，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Kong Fan, courtesy name Fayan, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Fan, styled Fayan, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖景偉，齊散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jingwei was Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jingwei was Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary under Qi.

sentences.zh: 祖滔，梁海鹽令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tao was Magistrate of Haiyan under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tao was magistrate of Haiyan under Liang.

sentences.zh: 父岱，曆職清顯。

translations.literal: His father Dai held a succession of pure, eminent offices.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dai held a succession of pure, eminent offices.

sentences.zh: 隋師將濟江，群官請為備防，文慶沮壞之，後主未決。

translations.literal: When the Sui armies were about to cross the river, the ministers petitioned for defensive preparations, but Wenqing obstructed and ruined the plan, and the Later Lord could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui armies were about to cross the river, the ministers petitioned for defensive preparations, but Wenqing obstructed and ruined the plan, and the Later Lord could not decide.

sentences.zh: 範奏曰：「長江天塹，古來限隔，虜軍豈能飛度？

translations.literal: Fan memorialized: "The Yangzi has been a heavenly barrier since antiquity, dividing north from south—how could the enemy army fly across?
translations.idiomatic: Fan memorialized, "The Yangzi has been a heavenly barrier since antiquity, dividing north from south—how could the enemy army fly across?

sentences.zh: 邊將欲作功勞，妄言事急。

translations.literal: The frontier commanders wish to claim merit and falsely say the situation is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier commanders wish to claim merit and falsely say the situation is urgent.

sentences.zh: 臣自恨位卑，虜若能來，定作太尉公矣。」

translations.literal: I regret only that my rank is low; if the barbarians can come, I am certain to be made Grand Marshal Duke.
translations.idiomatic: I regret only that my rank is low; if the barbarians can come, I am certain to be made Grand Marshal Duke.

sentences.zh: 或妄言北軍馬死，範曰：「此是我馬，何因死去。」

translations.literal: When someone falsely reported that the northern army's horses were dying, Fan said: "Those are my horses—why should they die?
translations.idiomatic: When someone falsely reported that the northern army's horses were dying, Fan said, "Those are my horses—why should they die?

sentences.zh: 後主笑以為然，故不深備。

translations.literal: The Later Lord laughed and agreed; hence he made no thorough preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord laughed and agreed; hence he made no thorough preparations.

sentences.zh: 尋而隋將賀若弼陷南徐州，執城主莊元始，韓擒陷南豫州，敗水軍都督高文泰。

translations.literal: Soon the Sui general He Ruobi took South Xuzhou and captured the city commander Zhuang Yuanshi; Han Qin took South Yuzhou and defeated the naval commander Gao Wentai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Sui general He Ruobi took South Xuzhou and captured the city commander Zhuang Yuanshi; Han Qin took South Yuzhou and defeated the naval commander Gao Wentai.

sentences.zh: 范與中領軍魯廣達頓于白塔寺。

translations.literal: Fan, together with Central Army Commander Lu Guangda, encamped at White Pagoda Monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, together with Central Army Commander Lu Guangda, encamped at White Pagoda Monastery.

sentences.zh: 後主多出金帛，募人立功，范素于武士不接，莫有至者，唯負販輕薄多從之，高麗、百濟、昆侖諸夷並受督。

translations.literal: The Later Lord offered gold and silk in abundance to enlist men for merit; Fan, who had never been close to warriors, found none came—only peddlers and idle riffraff followed him in great number, and Koreans, men of Baekje, and Kunlun foreigners all served under his command.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord offered gold and silk in abundance to enlist men for merit; Fan, who had never been close to warriors, found none came—only peddlers and idle riffraff followed him in great number, and Koreans, men of Baekje, and Kunlun foreigners all served under his command.

sentences.zh: 時任蠻奴請不戰，而己度江攻其大軍。

translations.literal: At the time Ren Manu asked to avoid battle and cross the river himself to attack the main enemy host.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ren Manu asked to avoid battle and cross the river himself to attack the main enemy host.

sentences.zh: 又司馬消難言於後主曰：「弼若登高舉烽，與韓擒相應，鼓聲交震，人情必離。

translations.literal: Sima Xiaonan also told the Later Lord: "If Ruobi raises beacon fires on high and Han Qin answers, with drums thundering in reply, the people's hearts will surely scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiaonan also told the Later Lord, "If Ruobi raises beacon fires on high and Han Qin answers, with drums thundering in reply, the people's hearts will surely scatter.

sentences.zh: 請急遣兵北據蔣山，南斷淮水，質其妻子，重其賞賜。

translations.literal: I ask that troops be urgently sent north to hold Mount Jiang and south to cut the Huai River, taking their wives and children as hostages and loading rewards upon them.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that troops be urgently sent north to hold Mount Jiang and south to cut the Huai River, taking their wives and children as hostages and loading rewards upon them.

sentences.zh: 陛下以精兵萬人，守城莫出。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with ten thousand picked troops, should hold the city and not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, with ten thousand picked troops, should hold the city and not go out.

sentences.zh: 不過十日，食盡，二將之頭可致闕下。」

translations.literal: Within ten days their provisions will be exhausted, and the heads of the two generals can be brought beneath the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days their provisions will be exhausted, and the heads of the two generals can be brought beneath the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 范冀欲立功，志在於戰，乃曰：「司馬消難狼子野心，任蠻奴淮南傖士，語並不可信。」

translations.literal: Fan, eager for merit and intent on fighting, then said: "Sima Xiaonan has the heart of a wolf cub; Ren Manu is a Huai River peasant soldier—their words are none of them to be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Fan, eager for merit and intent on fighting, then said, "Sima Xiaonan has the heart of a wolf cub; Ren Manu is a Huai River peasant soldier—their words are none of them to be trusted."

sentences.zh: 事遂不行。

translations.literal: The proposal was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 隋軍既逼，蠻奴又欲為持久計，範又奏：「請作一決，當為官勒石燕然。」

translations.literal: With the Sui army pressing close, Manu again wished to plan for a protracted defense, but Fan once more memorialized: "Let us fight one decisive battle; I shall have a stele carved on Mount Yanran.
translations.idiomatic: With the Sui army pressing close, Manu again wished to plan for a protracted defense, but Fan once more memorialized, "Let us fight one decisive battle; I shall have a stele carved on Mount Yanran for the state.

sentences.zh: 後主從之。

translations.literal: The Later Lord followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord agreed.

sentences.zh: 明日，範以其徒居中，以抗隋師，未陣而北，範脫身遁免。

translations.literal: The next day, Fan placed his followers in the center to resist the Sui army; before the battle lines were formed they fled north, and Fan slipped away and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Fan drew up his followers in the center to face the Sui army, but before the lines could be formed they broke and fled northward; Fan alone slipped away and escaped.

sentences.zh: 尋與後主俱入長安。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered Chang'an together with the Later Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered Chang'an together with the Later Lord.

sentences.zh: 初，晉王廣所戮陳五佞人，範與散騎常侍王瑳、王儀、御史中丞沈瓘，過惡未彰，故免。

translations.literal: At first, among the five fawning men of Chen executed by Prince of Jin Guang, Fan along with Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Chuo, Wang Yi, and Supervising Censor Shen Guan had crimes not yet exposed, and so were spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jin Guang executed Chen's five favorite flatterers, Fan along with Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Chuo, Wang Yi, and Supervising Censor Shen Guan were spared, for their crimes had not yet come to light.

sentences.zh: 及至長安，事並露，隋文帝以其奸佞諂惑，並暴其過惡，名為四罪人，流之遠裔，以謝吳、越之人。

translations.literal: When they reached Chang'an, the whole affair came to light; Emperor Wen of Sui, because of their treachery, flattery, and deluding influence, exposed all their crimes, named them the Four Criminals, and exiled them to remote regions to appease the people of Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Once they reached Chang'an, everything came to light. Emperor Wen of Sui, judging them treacherous flatterers who had led their ruler astray, publicly exposed their crimes, branded them the Four Criminals, and banished them to distant regions as amends to the people of Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 瑳、儀並琅邪人。

translations.literal: Chuo and Yi were both men of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo and Yi were both natives of Langye.

sentences.zh: 瑳刻薄貪鄙，忌害才能。

translations.literal: Chuo was harsh, greedy, and base, and jealous of men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo was harsh, greedy, and mean-spirited, and envied anyone with ability.

sentences.zh: 儀候意承顏，傾巧側媚，又獻其二女，以求親昵。

translations.literal: Yi watched expressions and flattered to please, poured forth cleverness and obsequious charm, and also offered his two daughters to seek intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Yi watched every mood and flattered accordingly, deploying all his cunning in sycophantic display, and even offered up his two daughters to win favor.

sentences.zh: 瓘險慘苛酷，發言邪諂，故同罪焉。

translations.literal: Guan was vicious, cruel, and harsh; his words were perverse and flattering—hence he shared their punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was vicious and pitiless in his cruelty, and his speech was warped and fawning—so he received the same sentence.

translations.literal: Commentary
translations.idiomatic: Commentary

sentences.zh: 論曰：自宋中世以來，宰禦朝政，萬機碎密，不關外司。

translations.literal: The commentary says: From the mid-Song period onward, favorites controlled court government; myriad affairs were fragmented and minute and did not involve the outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary observes: From the mid-Song period onward, court favorites controlled the government; the myriad affairs of state were broken into minute fragments that never passed through the regular ministries.

sentences.zh: 尚書八座五曹，各有恆任，系以九卿六府，事存副職。

translations.literal: The Eight Seats and Five Bureaus of the Secretariat each had fixed duties; linked with the Nine Ministers and Six Offices, affairs were held in duplicate posts.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat's Eight Seats and Five Bureaus each had their fixed duties, supported by the Nine Ministers and Six Offices in parallel posts—but in name only.

sentences.zh: 至於冠冕搢紳，任疏人貴，伏奏之務既寢，趨走之勞亦息。

translations.literal: As for capped officials and girdled gentry, their duties grew remote while their persons grew honored; the business of presenting memorials while prostrate had already ceased, and the labor of running about also ended.
translations.idiomatic: As for the crowned and girdled officials, their duties grew ever more remote even as their persons grew ever more honored; the work of kneeling to present memorials had long since ceased, and the bustle of running errands had quieted as well.

sentences.zh: 關宣所寄，屬當事有所歸。

translations.literal: What passed through gate and proclamation was entrusted, so that when matters arose there was someone to whom they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gate business and imperial pronouncements were entrusted to them, so that whenever something arose, there was always someone at hand to handle it.

sentences.zh: 通驛內外，切自音旨。

translations.literal: Dispatches connected inside and outside; all sprang from the ruler's words and intent.
translations.idiomatic: Couriers linked court and countryside, and everything turned on the sovereign's own words and will.

sentences.zh: 若夫竭忠盡節，仕子恒圖，隨方致用，明君盛典，舊非本舊，因新以成舊者也，狎非先狎，因疏以成狎者也。

translations.literal: Devotion and integrity are what officials always aspire to, and employing men according to their strengths is the enlightened ruler's great standard—but what was once not long-standing intimacy became intimacy through novelty, and what was once not prior familiarity became familiarity through gradual approach.
translations.idiomatic: Devotion and integrity are what every official aspires to, and putting men to use according to their gifts is the enlightened ruler's highest art—yet what had not been old intimacy became intimacy through novelty, and what had not been prior closeness became closeness through gradual cultivation.

sentences.zh: 而任隔疏情，殊塗一致，權歸近狎，異世同揆。

translations.literal: Yet though duties were divided and feelings remote, different paths led to one outcome: power returned to those close and intimate; different ages shared the same measure.
translations.idiomatic: Though their duties were formally separate and their rank distant, every path led to the same end—power settled in the hands of those nearest and most intimate; age after age, the pattern was identical.

sentences.zh: 故環纓斂笏，俯仰晨昏，瞻幄坐而竦躬，陪蘭檻而高眄，探求恩色，習睹威顏，遷蘭變鮑，久而彌信。

translations.literal: Thus with jeweled tassels and tablets in hand, bowing morning and evening, gazing at the curtained throne and straightening their bodies, attending by the orchid balustrade and looking up in reverence, seeking out expressions of favor and growing accustomed to the august countenance—orchids turning to salted fish—over time trust only deepened.
translations.idiomatic: Thus cap tassels bound and tablets held, they bowed morning and evening; gazing at the curtained throne they straightened their backs, attending at the orchid balustrade with upturned eyes, searching out every sign of favor and growing used to the sovereign's august face—orchids slowly turning to salted fish—and the longer it lasted, the deeper the trust ran.

sentences.zh: 因城社之固，執開壅之機。

translations.literal: Relying on the solidity of the altars of state, they grasped the mechanisms of monopoly and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Resting on the solid foundations of state power, they seized control of every gate and choke point.

sentences.zh: 長主君世，振裘持領，賞罰事殷，能不踰漏，宮省咳唾，義必先知。

translations.literal: Dominating the ruler's reign, they shook the fur and held the collar; rewards and punishments were abundant, and not one could slip past them—even a cough or spit in palace or court, they necessarily knew first.
translations.idiomatic: They dominated the ruler's reign, pulling the strings from the collar; rewards and punishments flowed through their hands, and nothing leaked past them—even a cough or a whisper in the inner palace, they invariably heard of it first.

sentences.zh: 故窺盈縮于望景，獲驪珠于龍睡，坐歸聲勢，臥震都鄙。

translations.literal: Thus they read rise and fall from watching shadows on the sundial, obtained the pearl from the sleeping dragon, and sitting gathered power and prestige while reclining shook capital and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: They read the rise and fall of fortunes in the shifting shadows on the sundial, plucked the pearl from the sleeping dragon, and whether sitting or reclining gathered power that shook the capital and the provinces alike.

sentences.zh: 賄賂日積，苞苴歲通，富擬公侯，威行州郡。

translations.literal: Bribes accumulated daily, gift-bundles passed yearly; their wealth rivaled marquises and dukes, and their authority extended through prefectures and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Bribes piled up day by day, gift parcels flowed year after year; their wealth matched that of marquises and dukes, and their authority reached across every prefecture and commandery.

sentences.zh: 制局小司，專典兵力，雲陛天居，亙設蘭綺，羽林精卒，重屯廣衛。

translations.literal: The small offices of the arsenal bureau exclusively managed military strength; cloud steps and the heavenly dwelling were lined everywhere with orchid silks, and elite Feathered Forest troops heavily garrisoned the broad guards.
translations.idiomatic: The minor posts of the arsenal bureau held sole charge of military force; the cloud-white steps and heavenly palace were hung everywhere with orchid silks, and picked Feathered Forest troops massed in heavy garrisons throughout the broad inner guard.

sentences.zh: 至於元戎啟轍，武候還麾，遮迾清道，神行按轡，督察往來，馳騖輦轂，驅役分部，親承几案，領護所攝，示總成規。

translations.literal: When the commander-in-chief opened march, military guards returned banners, blocked roads and cleared the way, moved like spirits while holding reins, inspected comings and goings, galloped at the chariot hub, drove and assigned divisions, personally received desk documents, and oversaw what they commanded—displaying the appearance of overall control.
translations.idiomatic: When the commander-in-chief set out, military guards wheeled their banners, roads were blocked and cleared, they moved like spirits with reins in hand, inspected all who came and went, galloped beside the imperial carriage, drove men and assigned posts, personally received documents at the desk, and supervised every command under their charge—giving every appearance of holding the whole apparatus in their grasp.

sentences.zh: 若徵兵動眾，大興人役，優劇遠近，斷於外監之心，譴辱詆訶，恣於典事之口。

translations.literal: If troops were recruited and masses mobilized, if great corvée projects were launched, whether burdens were light or heavy near or far was decided by the outer director's whim; reproaches, insults, and berating were at the disposal of the officer in charge's mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When troops were levied and masses mobilized, when great public works were launched, whether the burden was light or crushing, near or far, rested on the outer director's whim; reproach, insult, and abuse poured freely from the mouths of the officers in charge.

sentences.zh: 抑符緩詔，奸偽非一，書死為生，請謁成市，左臂揮金，右手刊字，紙為銅落，筆由利染。

translations.literal: They suppressed tally-documents and delayed edicts; frauds were many—writing the dead as living, petition-visits became a market, the left arm waving gold and the right hand carving characters, paper falling like copper coins, the brush driven by profit.
translations.idiomatic: They suppressed official tallies and delayed edicts; fraud took countless forms—the living were written off as dead, petitioners crowded the streets like a marketplace, gold changed hands on the left while characters were carved on the right, paper fell like rain of copper cash, and every brushstroke was stained with profit.

sentences.zh: 故門同玉署，家號金穴，嬙媛侍女，燕、秦、蔡、鄭之聲，琁池碧梁，魚龍雀馬之翫，莫不充牣錦室，照徹青雲，害政傷人，於斯為切。

translations.literal: Thus their gates rivaled jade offices and their houses were called gold caves; concubines and serving girls with music of Yan, Qin, Cai, and Zheng; jade pools and blue-green beams, amusements of fish, dragons, sparrows, and horses—none failed to fill brocade chambers and shine through the blue clouds; harm to government and injury to men were nowhere more acute.
translations.idiomatic: Their gates rivaled the jade halls of office, their houses were called treasure vaults; concubines and serving girls performed the music of Yan, Qin, Cai, and Zheng; jade pools and azure beams, diversions of fish, dragons, sparrows, and horses—all of it overflowing brocade chambers and gleaming to the very clouds. Nowhere did misgovernment and human suffering cut deeper.

sentences.zh: 況乎主幼時昏，讒慝亦何可勝紀也。

translations.literal: How much more when the ruler was young and feeble-minded at the time—slander and wickedness, how could they all be recorded?
translations.idiomatic: And when the ruler was young and muddled besides, how could slander and villainy even be fully counted?
